Weak consumer demand and rising prices weighed heavily on the offline smartphone market in the recently-concluded Diwali festive season. According to industry body All India Mobile Retailers Association (AIMRA), mobile phone retailers saw sales volumes decline by 18-20% over the four-day period between Dhanteras (November 6) and the day after Diwali (November 9). However, overall sales value remained broadly in line with last year’s festive season on the back of higher average selling prices. Nevertheless, AIMRA noted that the “steeper contraction” in volumes squeezed margins and store profitability across mainline retail channels. The industry body also said that offline smartphone sales volumes in the seven days preceding Dhanteras plunged nearly 40% as consumers delayed purchases in anticipation of festive offers. However, the demand picked up as customer footfall grew during the four-day period. Giving a breakdown of the demand data, the report noted that urban consumers showed muted interest in upgrading devices, while Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets recorded stronger momentum – especially particularly in the mid-segment. Most purchases were concentrated in the ₹30,000-60,000 price band after offers, while the premium segment also saw healthy demand, as per the report. The sub-₹20,000 segment was particularly impacted by a shortage of fresh, competitive 5G models from leading brands. As a result, some value-conscious buyers shifted to brands such as HMD, Lava, Ai+, Tecno and itel, while others opted for pre-owned and refurbished devices to access higher specifications at lower prices. AIMRA also said that financing emerged as another constraint during the festive season. The industry body claimed that only 60-70% of logged loan applications were approved, leaving a significant share of prospective buyers unable to complete purchases due to tighter underwriting and CIBIL-related rejections. Performance also varied sharply across brands. Apple and Google Pixel saw strong demand, as did Xiaomi, which benefited from competitive pricing. Meanwhile, Vivo, OPPO and Samsung also maintained healthy sales by value but saw weaker unit volumes. Realme saw volumes plunge by over 50% across regions, as per AIMRA. “This drop was triggered by uncompetitive pricing compared to Xiaomi, Samsung, and Vivo, zero new festive launches, and unlucrative consumer schemes. Market acceptance above ₹40,000 remains weak, dimming its near-term outlook,” said the industry body. Why Are Smartphones Becoming Pricey? Largely to blame for the subdued festive season was price hikes by smartphone companies and rising commodity prices. This comes as the ongoing AI boom has dried up the supply of many critical components for entry-level and budget smartphone makers, which operate on razor-thin profit margins. This is because memory chips makers are actively prioritising the demand from data centres and AI infrastructure providers, where margins are higher. As a result, the per-device memory cost has already increased to $60-65, a 3X jump from around $20 in 2025, per a recent Jefferies report. As a result, the brokerage firm expects the prices of low-end smartphones to increase nearly 30%. Overall, consulting giant Deloitte expects the memory shortage to last until as late as 2030. To tide over this, smartphone makers have resorted to price hikes to pass on the higher component costs to consumers. Retail prices of existing smartphones have increased by as much 21% in India on an average, as per Counterpoint Research. The memory crisis has also particularly impacted the budget segment of the market, where manufacturers have limited room to absorb cost increases without sacrificing margins. This explains why India, a relatively price-sensitive market, has been heavily impacted. The trend is expected to hold going forward as well. Xiaomi has already signalled price increases of up to ₹4,000 across product categories, while other smartphone makers are preparing hikes of up to 15%. With festive footfall already moderating, the AIMRA expects sales volumes at mainline brick-and-mortar stores to contract by as much as 50% over the next three months.

The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes.
Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended.
His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive.
Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast in south-eastern Kenya.
In total, more than 400 bodies have been recovered. Many were severely decomposed and only 26 could be identified.
Mackenzie denied murder charges, saying he did not force the victims to starve, but the court rejected that argument.
The Shakahola tragedy has gripped Kenya since the discovery of mass graves in the forest more than three years ago.
It raised questions about how Mackenzie was able to continue operating despite being on the radar of the authorities since 2017, when police searched his premises.
In 2019, authorities shut down Mackenzie’s church and he relocated to the Shakahola forest, police said.
The case has also led to calls for tougher oversight of churches and other religious organisations in a country where religious faith plays a prominent role in public life.
Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, forbade cult members from sending their children to school and from going to hospital when they were ill, describing such institutions as satanic.
Cult members lived in makeshift homes of polythene sheeting and thatch that Mackenzie divided into areas with biblical names such as Jerusalem and Judea.
The plight of his followers began to emerge in March 2023, when a man told police his brother and wife had starved their children to death in the forest on Mackenzie’s orders.
Mackenzie was arrested but released on bail, after which relatives said he brought forward the date on which he told his followers the world would end. Police rearrested him and started combing through the forest more systematically and began exhuming mass graves.
Last month’s judgment covered 191 deaths while investigations into more than 200 other deaths are continuing.
Justice Diana Kavedza-Mochache said in a hearing lasting more than eight hours that in some cases children were isolated and denied food while their parents watched.
Mackenzie faces other charges over the forest deaths, including those of terrorism, which he has denied.
Prosecutors said that while he was in detention he also directed the deaths of 52 people in Kwa Binzaro village, about 18 miles from Shakahola. Mackenzie has pleaded not guilty in that case.

Raducanu to return at January's United Cup after injury absence
- Published
Emma Raducanu will make her return to tennis in the United Cup team competition in Australia in the first week of 2027.
Britain's 2021 US Open champion has not played since June because of a stress fracture of the shin.
Raducanu was beaten by Croatia’s Donna Vekic in her first grass-court final at Queen's Club on 14 June, but had to pull out of Wimbledon on the eve of her opening match just 14 days later.
The 23-year-old contemplated playing a couple of events in Asia this autumn but, by delaying her return until January, she will be able to use a special ranking of 38 to enter tournaments.
A special ranking is available to players who have been out with injury for at least six months. In Raducanu's case, it reflects her position in the world rankings after Wimbledon, as she received some prize money despite not playing a match there.
The current British number five will be able to use a special ranking to enter eight events next year, including two Grand Slams and five WTA 1000 tournaments.
Her actual ranking of 107 would likely be too low to make the main draw of January's Australian Open and most other WTA Tour events.
But with a special ranking, Raducanu will not only be assured of playing in Melbourne but also at the WTA 1000 events in Doha, Dubai, Indian Wells and Miami which follow in February and March.
The entry deadline for the United Cup passed on Monday, shortly after Raducanu had her application for a special ranking approved.
A ranking of 38 will make her the British number one for the purposes of this event, giving her the chance to play alongside Arthur Fery in a competition featuring 18 national teams.
Francesca Jones, Jan Choinski and doubles players Neal Skupski and Olivia Nicholls complete the British team for the tournament, which takes place from 1-10 January.
Britain will play Australia and France in their group matches in Sydney, and Raducanu can expect to be face current top-40 players Talia Gibson and Diane Parry.

Raducanu made a gradual return to training in early September - and four months is a long time to train without any competitive action.
She may also not play any exhibitions between now and the end of the year but a spell of warm weather training is anticipated, with the Middle East a popular destination for players in the run-up to the Australian Open.
Recent practice sessions in London with head coach Andrew Richardson and LTA national coach Alex Ward have been increasing in intensity, according to observers.
But by the time Raducanu returns, she will have been on the sidelines for over six months. Playing a few tournaments in Asia would have helped her regain some match sharpness, and perhaps allowed for a faster start to 2027.
Her fellow Briton Sonay Kartal is a fine example, having enjoyed considerable success since returning from six months out with a stress fracture of the back in September.
After reaching the third round of the China Open in her first WTA Tour event back, she beat world number six Elina Svitolina and then world number 12 Belinda Bencic on her way to the Wuhan Open final.
Kartal says there were a "lot of conversations" about where she should make a return.
"I think I wanted to just go straight in. I trusted that I would be able to get my level back, I just didn't know how quickly," the 25-year-old said.
"But I still think there is a long way to go. I can produce the level, but can I sustain it?
"Rehab is draining, and the body is not used to a lot of matches on the tour, so I do feel the aches and the pains from that."
There will only be 24 candles on Raducanu’s birthday cake later this week, but there is no escaping the amount of time she has missed since her stunning New York victory as a teenage qualifier.
She has averaged just 31 matches a season in the five years since that triumph. Players with aspirations to be inside the world's top 20 would hope to play around twice that number.
Elena Rybakina, for example, played 68 matches across 20 tournaments this year as she rose to the top of the world rankings for the first time.
By contrast, Raducanu played just 21 matches, losing in the second round of the Australian Open and the first round at Roland Garros.
Last year, Raducanu contested a career-best 50 matches, and earlier this year rose to 23 in the rankings shortly after reaching the final in the Romanian city of Cluj.
But her early preparation was affected by bone bruising of the foot, and she did not play for two months between March and May because of a post-viral illness picked up in Cluj.
Raducanu said a stress fracture of the shin was only confirmed after a final scan on the night before Wimbledon. But in her desperation to play, she had continued to train at times in the run-up to the championships, when medical advice had suggested that might be unwise.

In a reddit AMA on Friday, in between jokes about gay bears and JD Vance’s potential username being CushionCasanova, Grindr CEO George Arison answered a question about the economy. He didn’t hold back.
“Inflation is terrible, and there’s a massive affordability crisis in this country that our government has ignored since at least 2020,” he wrote in the r/wallstreetbets subreddit, where, following the release of the company’s quarterly earnings report, he took questions from users.
It was a startling admission from the man whose company is about to release a subscription offering intended to price out most Grindr users. On November 17, Edge, a “premium tier” with some AI-powered features costing $120 a month, will be available to members worldwide, according to the report. Early access opened today.
The document suggests that Edge will help users find connections “with less effort” and will include a personalized recommendation feature, Insights, to “understand compatibility and the likelihood of a reply,” as well as Reconnect, which “brings past connections back into view.” The app will have an entirely new design, interface, and icon intended to create a different experience for users willing to foot the high price tag.
But even if you can afford it, you may not get in. As with Raya, an invite-only app where some people have been on the wait list for as long as seven years, the company is planning to turn Edge into a digital gated community of sorts: Sign-ups will be limited to 1 percent of global monthly users.
The goal is to “deliberately [manage] the growth of the Edge community to preserve exclusivity” for “a select community” who can pay “meaningfully more,” the report indicated. According to figures from the company, only 1.4 million of its current 16 million users pay to use Grindr.
Edge’s official rollout comes following pilot programs in Australia, New Zealand, Canada, and the US, and a year’s worth of speculation about how much it would cost and what exactly would separate it from other apps that provide comparable features at a lower price.
“These VIP tiers make me think of [it as a] digital version of expensive hustler bars,” one user said on Instagram. “The men who will pay hundreds for access are rarely the hot men you would log on for.”
Grindr is the world’s largest dating app for gay, bi, and trans people, but it has consistently struggled with concerns over data privacy and user safety. And as it unveils its latest upsell, many members say the app’s fundamental infrastructure remains broken.
“Grindr is a top-tier example of enshitification and predatory monetization,” one person wrote in the reddit AMA from last week. “You need to stop with the intrusive ads and start getting in touch with reality,” posted another.
In September, the company agreed to a $35 million class action settlement over allegedly sharing users’ HIV status and testing information with third-party vendors; the details of the settlement included no admission of liability on Grindr’s behalf. That same month, Grindr acquired the telehealth company Freddie, which helps people get access to the HIV-prevention medication PrEP. The purchase builds on Arison’s investment into health care and turning the app into a social network. Currently, Grindr sells erectile dysfunction pills and GLP-1 weight-loss medication through its Woodwork program.
Critics will likely argue that pivoting to luxury dating in an economy where more and more people are struggling isn’t great optics, but Arison is betting that improved features and a “deliberately limited membership” will create opportunity for “substantially higher pricing over time,” the report noted.

After knife-edge vote, New Zealand parties put off coalitions talks
- Published
Who will form New Zealand's next government remains uncertain after the country's national election on Saturday, with final results not due for another couple of weeks.
It's the tightest vote that the country has seen in years, with the incumbent National Party and opposition Labour Party neck-and-neck in terms of party vote share.
In terms of seats, a National-led conservative coalition, which includes the Act Party and NZ First, are projected to win a combined 67 seats - giving them a narrow one-seat majority.
As questions about other coalitions swirl, party leaders are remaining tight-lipped, saying they would wait for the final results before formal discussions.
Major parties on both sides of the political aisle were "likely dissatisfied with their campaigns", Max Rashbrooke, adjunct senior research fellow at the Victoria University of Wellington, told the BBC.
The opposition Labour Party, led by Chris Hipkins, ran an election campaign that "seems to have inspired few voters", despite going up against Christopher Luxon, a "historically unpopular prime minister", Rashbrooke said.
On the other hand, he added, the incumbent National Party also "failed to spark enthusiasm" even though it "should have been safe" given the country hasn't seen a one-term government in more than 50 years.
The election dealt a huge blow to National with the loss of some of its most senior lawmakers, including Finance Minister Nicola Willis, Justice Minister Paul Goldsmith, Transport Minister Chris Bishop and House Speaker Gerry Brownlee.
Act Party leader David Seymour has expressed interest in the finance minister portfolio, telling news outlet Stuff that National must recognise the voters' message and let its coalition partners play a bigger role.
"The government barely survived, it must now put its best foot forward in every step," he said.
The big winners of election night were "the more radical minor parties", Rashbrooke said.
The left-leaning Greens and the right-wing libertarian Act Party both saw new highs this election, while the Opportunity Party, a fledgling centrist party, scored a breakout victory. Having previously failed three times at getting into Parliament, it's now projected to get seven seats.
Opportunity's incoming lawmakers, including leader Qiulae Wong, arrived at New Zealand's parliament on Monday morning, for the start of what Wong said would be a week of "induction stuff".
Opportunity, which has rejected traditional political divisions, has said it's open to forming a coalition with either major party.
Whichever coalition they join, though, they would "really need to be comfortable with the overall direction the government is going in", Wong told reporters on Monday.
Wong said that although she has received calls of congratulations from Labour's Hipkins and the Greens' Chlöe Swarbrick, they have not had any discussions about coalitions.
Luxon, who had previously ruled out working with Opportunity, told public broadcaster RNZ on Monday that he wanted to talk to Wong "shortly".
Counting is still underway for nearly 400,000 "special votes", which includes those from overseas voters and people outside of their electorate.
These make up 14% of total votes, and are likely to be important in the final count.
"They tend to lean left, as voters casting special votes tend to be younger and more likely to be renters - and therefore more likely to be living outside their electorate," senior politics lecturer Claire Timperley told the BBC on election night.
"The overseas vote might be more likely than usual to be disaffected by the current coalition, given we've seen increasing numbers of New Zealanders moving overseas as a result of cost-of-living challenges."
Faced with a stagnating economy and challenging job market, a record number of Kiwis are moving overseas in search of better career opportunities. More than 114,000 people migrated out of the country in the year leading up to August.
Young people the BBC spoke to ahead of the election said they were "tired" and "cynical" about the future - part of what polling shows is a general grim mood across the country.
"In New Zealand as elsewhere, politics is splintering. But which parties ultimately benefit remains unclear for now," said Rashbrooke.
Final election results are expected on 27 November, with the official confirmation of MPs set for 3 December.

Dovish BOJ policymaker Asada pushes back against early rate hike
NAGASAKI, Japan, Nov 12 : Dovish Bank of Japan policymaker Toichiro Asada pushed back against calls within the board for a near-term interest rate hike, arguing on Thursday that premature rate hikes could hurt growth and push down underlying inflation.
While an overshoot of inflation above the BOJ's 2 per cent target could have adverse effects on the economy, there was also a risk the effect of past and future rate hikes may weigh on economic activity and underlying inflation, Asada said in a speech to business leaders in Nagasaki, southern Japan.
Welcoming data showing real wages turned positive since the turn of 2026, Asada said growth and consumption have lacked momentum.
"I believe the recent price increases have not necessarily been driven by demand factors," said Asada, who dissented on the BOJ's decisions to raise interest rates in June and September.
"In this sense, I consider it necessary for the Bank to give due consideration to the pace of any policy rate hikes," he said, stressing the need to avoid cooling growth with too-fast rate hikes.

Lucid CEO says the company didn't know where its own cars were
Gaps in its logistics system caused the EV maker to lose orders.
Lucid, the California-based Tesla rival that makes luxury EVs like the Air and Gravity, has an interesting excuse for its third quarter earnings underperformance. The company said it lost sales due to inventory control issues, with CEO Silvio Napoli admitting in an earnings call that sometimes "we did not even know where cars were." That chaos resulted in slow delivery times up to two weeks that caused Lucid to lose orders from impatient buyers.
The company doesn't have millions of cars to keep track of like Tesla, either. Lucid built just 2,954 vehicles last quarter and delivered 3,806, down seven percent from the year before. Building fewer cars than it sold helped it reduce inventory, but it still had $1.22 billion worth on the books at the end of September.
With its logistics issues, Lucid's sales suffered like Tesla's did when the latter started ramping up the Model 3. Elon Musk's company had to take drastic measures to solve supply issues (like building its own car carriers and buying trucking companies), but once it did, sales took off.
Lucid's Napoli suggested that its latest fixes to shipping problems will have a similar effect by allowing the commercial team to "sell the cars that we know can be available on the day for the customers who require it." With that, along with a growing US EV market due to high gas prices (plus a deal it recently cut with robotaxi company Bolt), the company has positive expectations for the latter half of 2026.
Fixing its supply chain won't solve Lucid's other problems, though, like quality control issues and customer service complaints. The other tiny issue is that the automaker lost $831 million last quarter on revenue of just $350 million, due to cost of making each vehicle that far exceeds the selling price. However, that didn't discourage the company's primary investor, the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), from injecting an additional $1.75 billion into Lucid.

Australia doomed to live with stench of sandpapergate
- Published
There are stories that can damage reputations, tarnish legacies and put asterisks next to achievements.
Never-ending sagas, claim and counterclaim, one word against another.
Are Pep Guardiola's trophies at Manchester City rendered worthless by financial rule breaches? Would either of the Houston Astros or Boston Red Sox have won the World Series without sign stealing? How much fake blood was spilled by Harlequins?
Now, sandpapergate has morphed into Usman Khawaja's-book-gate, opening old wounds and asking questions that have hung over Australian cricket since Cameron Bancroft hid some DIY equipment in his jockstrap in 2018.
Published on Tuesday, Khawaja's autobiography – Sabr – is only suggesting what plenty have suspected for the past eight years.
It always seemed likely that Bancroft, Steve Smith and David Warner were not the only three members of the Australia camp with knowledge of the sandpaper plot.
Careful with his words, perhaps for legal reasons, Khawaja has said enough to reignite a row that once consumed the entire nation of Australia. Crucially, the former batter has not named individuals and, in the opinion of Cricket Australia (CA), not presented enough evidence to merit a new investigation.
It was Nathan Lyon who once said Australia know how to "headbutt the line, but we won't go over it". Khawaja has headbutted the line of whistle-blowing, without taking a full toot.
There are some key quotes from Khawaja, taken from the autobiography and his public statements of the past few days.
Writing in Sabr, Khawaja says: "I'm going to use the term 'we' throughout this chapter, because 'we' are team Australia – although in this book I'm not speaking on behalf of anyone but myself. This will be my recollection of events."
In a video posted on Instagram, he added: "You would have seen when I mentioned it was all of us, that's implying that whether we like it or not, we are all responsible for what happened together. As a team, we need to take that collectively. That is all."
Then, to ABC on Tuesday: "I'm not here to go on a witch hunt. All I've ever wanted is for us to take accountability as a team."
Rather than directly accusing his team-mates, Khawaja is asking the Australians present in Cape Town to share the blame that was given to Smith, Warner and Bancroft. An individual can be culpable for what happened, even if they were not the one to directly rub sandpaper on the red leather.
Khawaja has also explained that much of his motivation for telling this story comes from loyalty to his childhood friend Warner.
Warner has had his say and, like Khawaja, has not named anyone else he feels should be implicated.
There are questions as to why neither man has spoken up over the past eight years. If they felt strongly, they could have come forward at any time, even if Khawaja is proved correct in his claim he was not interviewed in the original investigation.
Then again, there was the issue of squad harmony, loyalty to their friends and protecting their places in the Australia team. Warner may yet reveal more in the future, ditto for Smith and Bancroft.
This latest evidence has done little to shift views that were entrenched before Khawaja put pen to paper. Darren Lehmann, Australia coach at the time, has stuck to his story of denial, as has Mitchell Starc. Chadd Sayers, another seamer in the 2018 squad, has come out in support of Khawaja and Warner.
So far, so much stalemate.
It leaves the ball in the court of the other Australian players involved, the coaching staff and CA.
On Tuesday, CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said, with a straight face, he did not see "any compelling reason" to reopen the investigation into the ball-tampering saga.
What evidence could compel Greenberg to act? Even if Khawaja has not directly pointed the finger at anyone else in the dressing room that day, surely CA should be curious about the claims that are currently causing so much reputational damage, especially when Khawaja and Warner have called into question the rigour of the original investigation.
The Cape Town files have never been made public. In 2021, David Saker, an Australia assistant coach in 2018, called for them to be released. Now, Saker is not named but is among the staff Khawaja has implicated in the book by claiming a member of the backroom team encouraged Bancroft. That allegation alone surely merits further scrutiny by CA.
Of the players in the Australia XI on that Saturday at Newlands, three were punished; now Khawaja has accepted his share of responsibility, making four.
Tim Paine inherited the captaincy, a reign that ended in his own scandal. Mitchell Marsh remains an active player and is about to skipper Australia in the limited-overs series against England. Marsh will speak on Thursday. His brother Shaun was also in the team in Cape Town. That makes seven.
Then there are the four bowlers, possibly the greatest four-man attack ever assembled.
Starc, with more Test wickets than any other left-arm bowler in history. Lyon, the most successful orthodox finger-spinner in Test cricket. Josh Hazlewood, the reincarnation of Glenn McGrath. Pat Cummins, the clean-cut current Australia captain, an Ashes and World Cup-winning leader.
That they are still Australia's first-choice bowling unit is testament to their talent, longevity and desire. They remain as a quartet, hunting prizes that have previously eluded them over the coming year – an away Test series win in India, winning the Ashes in England.
As it stands, they are adhering to a joint-statement made in 2021 that they "did not know a foreign substance was taken on to the field".
The plausibility of elite bowlers not knowing a ball has been tampered with is up for debate. The quartet point to the fact the on-field umpires on the day did not see any reason to change the ball at the time. In contrast, Khawaja said the effects of sandpaper could leave swirls on the leather.
For Cummins, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon, champion bowlers, the insinuation hangs over them. It is hard to prove a negative. Perhaps the off-ramp is for the foursome to themselves call for a reopening of the investigation? It could clear their names.
As it stands, Australian cricket is stuck in a sandpaper limbo, a halfway house full of historical scandal, innuendo and unanswered questions. According to former captain Michael Clarke, further inaction would leave supporters unable to "trust what's real".
Perhaps there is another scenario, the unpalatable prospect of those at the top having no desire to open the door for fear of what might lie behind it. It is worth remembering that the past two Australia captains have lost the job in disgrace: Smith for sandpaper, Paine for sexting.
Is that worse than the status quo? Sandpaper is the stench Australian cricket cannot shake.

Following the temporary collapse of the fan fiction website A03, extremely horny millennial women are on the hunt for other ways to get their rocks off—and Regal Cinemas execs are more than happy to help.
On Tuesday, the movie theater chain announced that for one night only, on November 16, it will be screening 4DX versions of episodes 5 and 6 of Heated Rivalry, the smash-hit gay hockey show adapted from the bestselling novels by Rachel Reid that first aired on the Canadian network Crave but blasted into the mainstream when it came to HBO Max. The screenings will be at 59 theaters across the US, as well as a handful of theaters in Canada and the United Kingdom.
The screenings are intended to give fans the opportunity “to go to the cottage and really experience” Hollanov all over again, says Jack Grimes, senior director of alternative business development at Regal.
The 4DX screenings are upping the ante for the fan-favorite Heated Rivalry screenings, which have been selling out in movie theaters across the US for the past month. Though the series is widely available to stream, fans have flocked to theaters to shout along to t.a.T.u’s “All the Things She Said” during the club scene in episode four and post photos of the Heated Rivalry–themed popcorn buckets featuring stars Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams in a sweaty, shirtless embrace. Thus far, such public displays of down bad-ness have been incredibly lucrative: as of November 8, Regal has earned $1.4 million from its limited theatrical release, per Variety’s reporting.
Still, Heated Rivalry isn’t an obvious candidate for a 4DX release. Originating in South Korea in 2009, 4DX technology provides an immersive experience for the viewer, such as motion-enabled chairs; environmental effects like wind, snow, and rain; or even scents, such as the smell of gunpowder or explosives during battle scenes. It’s mostly been used for big-budget action-adventure movies and thrillers such as The Odyssey and Avatar: The Way of Water.
Recently, however, there’s been increasing demand for 4DX big-screen releases for not just conventional action movies but also straightforward dramas, comedies, and even romances. Put another way, there’s evidence that a not-insubstantial number of the filmgoing public would like nothing more than a two-hour license to hump their seats.
For instance, as the result of what was essentially an extremely online in-joke, last month the film distributor Black Bear hosted 4DX screenings of the romantic black comedy Wicker, starring Olivia Colman as a woman who falls in love with a straw-plaited man (Alexander Skarsgaard). The screening featured such immersive special effects as water splashing in the audience’s faces when Colman’s character empties out her chamber pot, as well as synchronized motion-activated “thrusts” in the audience’s seats during sex scenes.
Grimes tells WIRED that the idea to produce 4DX Heated Rivalry screenings was in part inspired by the intense social media response to Wicker.
“We think the demographic overlap is really significant between the two,” he says. “They’re both very female-driven, in terms of what the viewership looks like.” The sales numbers for the Heated Rivalry screenings “emphasized that we needed to bring this to life,” Grimes says.
In general, filmmakers are increasingly becoming more creative about how they incorporate 4DX effects into their work. According to a Vulture interview with Jaehyun Jeong and Jaesang Yoon, two producers for the special effects company CJ 4DPlex, Paul Thomas Anderson specifically requested “sexual movements” for a scene in One Battle After Another in which Sean Penn’s character masturbates.
When asked about which specific effects will be used for Heated Rivalry, Grimes says CJ 4DPlex is in the process of coding the 4DX version, so he couldn’t say for sure. But he says it will likely “lean a lot into the motion effects,” albeit “where it makes sense to do so and where it's going to be tasteful to do so.”
Does that mean the chairs will thrust during sex scenes, as some randy fans have speculated? “I mean, it's, it's something that we saw in Wicker, so I wouldn't say that it's out of a stretch of imagination to say it's going to happen here,” Grimes says.
Unfortunately, the effects will perhaps not be quite as explicit as they were in Wicker, as it’s worth noting that episodes 5 and 6 are significantly less graphic than those earlier in the season. But it’s still tempting to consider how, exactly, Regal plans to incorporate special effects into the screening. Chirping crickets during the cottage scenes? Ice chips flying around when Kip rushes down to the rink to make out with Scott to the adrenaline-pumping percussive strains of “I’ll Believe in Anything”? An unidentified substance spraying in the audience’s faces when Ilya finishes off Shane while he’s on a call? The mind reels.

A group of around 40 men allegedly ambushed a house church in Rayan village in West Bengal’s Purba Bardhaman district on November 1, and physically assaulted the pastor and several Christian worshippers during a Sunday prayer service. The attackers accused the congregation of converting Hindus by luring them with incentives, and also accused them of running a ‘honey trap’.
Survivors told Alt News that they were forced to chant ‘Jai Sri Ram’, and were told, “This is a Hindu area; worshipping Jesus will not be tolerated”.
Several worshippers sustained severe injuries after the attack. Survivors said they were left traumatised without administrative protection or assurance. A written complaint was submitted at Burdwan police station. However, the survivors alleged that they were forced into withdrawing the complaint as attackers entered the police station and threatened to kill the complainant.
Alt News spoke to pastor Chottu Ruidas, who was leading the Sunday prayer service, and other survivors of the attack. Recounting the incident, Ruidas said the congregation had assembled at Sushanta Majila’s house around 10 am, and the service was nearing its conclusion, with the worshippers participating in communion, when a group of approximately 40 men descended on the house church, raising ‘Jai Sri Ram’ slogans.
According to Ruidas, Bisweshwar Choudhury, an influential and wealthy resident of the village who is known for helping people in need, was part of the group. He approached Ruidas during the prayer service and allegedly slapped him.
“Thereafter, the goons accompanying Choudhury started beating us mercilessly,” Ruidas told Alt News. “They slapped us, kicked us and beat us with the bamboo sticks they were carrying. They even took off their belts and whipped us.”
Ruidas said a 17-year-old boy sustained a severe head injury, leaving him bleeding profusely. “The goons told him, ‘We have treated you. Now go to a doctor and get it fixed,” he recounted.
The attackers allegedly dragged worshippers out of the house and beaten up. Those who attempted to seek refuge in neighbouring homes were pursued and assaulted, Ruidas said.
“After the goons beat us, the other attendees locked me inside a kitchen to keep me safe. But they broke open the door and dragged me out. My elder sister hugged me and fell to the ground while trying to protect me. But they continued kicking us. My sister eventually fell unconscious, and I had to take her to a nearby dispensary,” he said.
Ruidas told Alt News that he had attempted to contact police while hiding inside the kitchen but could not get through. He subsequently informed Pastor Jose Bernard, who then contacted the cops.
Bernard told Alt News that he called the Burdwan police station two to three times, but the police allegedly did not take the matter seriously. He eventually dialled the emergency helpline, 112, following which police personnel reached the village.
Bernard said his wife and minor daughter were also among the worshippers present at the congregation. By the time police reached the location, several miscreants had fled the scene. He claimed that when police entered the premises, the remaining miscreants accused the worshippers of having picked a fight with them.
Then, according to the pastor, instead of taking action against the attackers, police detained 20 women, three minors, and eight men from the Christian congregation.
Bernard categorically denied allegations of forceful conversion or conversion through inducement.
Worshippers Detained, Threatened by Accused inside Police Station
The detainees were first taken to Bardhaman Medical College and Hospital, where a doctor examined them inside the vehicle. Then, they were taken to the police station and kept in two separate rooms.
Pastor Jose Bernard subsequently submitted a written complaint at the police station. However, shortly afterwards, a group of alleged attackers entered the police station, grabbed him by the collar and threatened him with dire consequences unless he withdrew the complaint. He alleged that this happened in the presence of police personnel.
“They entered the police station, grabbed me by the collar, physically intimidated me and threatened to kill me if I did not withdraw my complaint. And all of this happened in front of the police,” Bernard told Alt News.
According to Bernard, police merely told the men, “There are CCTV cameras here; leave the premises’. That’s all.”
Bernard said that the threats and intimidation eventually compelled him to withdraw the complaint. He told Alt News that he had pleaded with the miscreants and police to at least ensure that Christians in Rayan village would not be subjected to further harassment. “This is our government. A Hindu government. A Hindu country. Worshipping Jesus is not allowed. They have to bathe in the Ganga, and we will perform ‘ghar wapsi’,” Bernard recalled them saying.
Bernard further alleged that the inspector in-charge, Debabrata Mukherjee, questioned the congregation about why they had assembled to pray in the first place. When the attendees and Bernard attempted to reason, Mukherjee allegedly asked why they were taking such risks when people were being assaulted for doing so in several places.
Eventually, the women were released from the police station around 11 pm, while the men were released around 1 am.
Speaking to Alt News, Burdwan IC Debabrata Mukherjee denied the allegation that the attackers entered the police station and threatened Pastor Jose Bernard to withdraw the complaint.
He said, “They submitted a complaint and, after some time, retracted it. No one threatened them inside the police station,” adding that “Counter-complaints have been filed against them by locals.”
Asked why the injured were detained at police station for long hours, Mukherjee claimed their families hadn’t turned up to take them home.
The officer refused to answer further questions over phone.
Elderly Woman Assaulted at Home
Another attendee, Sagari Konai, managed to escape the initial attack and returned to her home. However, a group of men allegedly went to her residence and assaulted her. She sustained a fracture in her finger due to the assault, the pastors added.
Ruidas alleged that the men forced Konai to perform sit-ups while holding her ears and apologise for practising Christianity. She was also allegedly coerced into participating in Hindu rituals at a nearby temple.
Konai is an elderly widow who lives with her daughter.
The attack has left the survivors deeply shaken. Ruidas said that he was still in pain from the injuries he sustained and that he was afraid to return to his home in Rayan village. He is currently staying with Bernerd.
Bernerd, meanwhile, said the incident had a profound impact on his young daughter, who witnessed the violence firsthand.
“She has never been exposed to such brutal hatred unfolding before her eyes. I wonder whether these people are animals,” he said.

Russia-Ukraine talks turn to post-war security but end without breakthrough
- Published
Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine have concluded after a second day.
Although the American side said they saw "some openings", there was no hint of any breakthroughs to end the nearly five year-long war sparked by Russia's invasion.
Davyd Arakhamia from Ukraine's negotiating team said that this round of talks - the first since February - "was one of the hardest."
"I believe the Russians came with very strict directives, so it was extremely difficult to soften the discussion," he said. But he added that he felt "good momentum" and urged for a second round of talks to be organised as soon as possible.
Both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large-scale prisoner of war exchange was in the works and could be carried out soon.
After the talks it was announced that on Thursday US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner - President Donald Trump's son-in-law - would travel to Moscow to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, and then to Dublin to speak to Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.
This latest round of talks had been framed as centred around the "security architecture" of Europe.
For Kyiv, this may include reassurances that allies will come to its aid if Ukraine comes under attack again, despite the country not being a Nato member.
For Moscow, it is likely to include a limit to the influence of Nato in eastern Europe - a central concern for the Kremlin since the alliance's eastward expansion.
Earlier this week Kushner said the US hoped to "create a new framework" of security between Ukraine, Russia and Europe that could "secure lasting peace", while Kremlin negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said the world needed a "new" and "fair" security system.
Ukraine and Europe have long been concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin.
Representatives of Britain, Nato and various EU countries were also in Abu Dhabi and met with US and Ukrainian negotiators, but the Kremlin - with whom the EU does not officially communicate - said its delegation had not had any contact with them.
Moscow has been dismissive of European involvement, although Europeans have long argued that they are central to any post-war dynamics on their continent.
Many - particularly in eastern Europe - feel their security is linked to that of Ukraine. Agreements cannot be implemented "if no consensus can be reached among Nato members," a German government spokesperson said on Wednesday.
Kushner said the US was keen to bring the Europeans on board and said that getting them "added to the format" would be on the agenda for his talks with Putin.
There is also disagreement on whether discussions on a future security framework should be preceded by a ceasefire, as the Europeans and Kyiv would want, or whether the fighting only stops after an agreement has been reached, as the Kremlin has insisted.
Any agreement on a peacetime security framework, however, is contingent on the war ending, Kushner noted. But that cannot occur "until there's an agreement on territory and on all other bilateral issues," he added.
Since talks began last year, a core obstacle to any settlement has been Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas.
This matter was the "hardest", Kushner acknowledged, while Zelensky's chief of staff and negotiator Kyrylo Budanov refused to be drawn on whether Russia was still demanding a Ukrainian withdrawal from the region.
"These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex," Kushner said. "The reality is there is no trust right now between the sides and that is to be expected after a conflict like this."

She lost her sight - now she is fighting to make history for Africa
- Published
Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon only took up sambo this year, but the Nigerian has already secured her place in the history of the martial art.
The sport shares strong roots with judo and wrestling, combining techniques such as hip and leg throws to take opponents to the mat, where they can be pinned.
Originally developed by the Soviet Union's Red Army in the 1920s, it was officially recognised as a combat sport by USSR officials in 1938.
Competing at the 2026 World Sambo Cup in Armenia, Suleimon defeated Uzbekistan's Charos Ortikova in the final of the women's 54kg category to claim victory on her international debut.
It was the first time that women with visual impairments had been included at the competition.
"Being the first female blind sambist in the world to win the gold medal makes me great," the 32-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.
"This is my first time in sambo and God crowned my efforts."
Suleimon's achievement was part of a breakthrough moment for African women in the sport. She and compatriot Elizabeth Aseso, who competed in the 59kg category, were among the pioneering sambists representing the continent in Yerevan.
For Suleimon, her gold medal is a reward for the hard work over many years which has seen her move from athletics to judo and now to the top of the international sambo podium.
"I really benefit a lot from sports and, despite my blindness, I achieve a lot," she said.
"If I [were] not blind, I don't think I would be at this level. I believe I will achieve even more."
From darkness to double glory
Suleimon's journey to becoming a champion has been marked by hardship and a determination to rebuild her life.
After failed surgeries she lost her sight in 2009 because of glaucoma, an eye condition that damages the optic nerve and can lead to permanent loss of vision.
The change in her circumstances affected her relationships, leaving her feeling isolated at a time when she needed support the most.
"People looked down on me. I would just stay indoors and cry," she explained.
"So many friends left me. They stopped communicating with me."
Her life began to take a different direction after she attended a vocational training centre for blind people in Lagos.
Through a friend, she was introduced to a para-athletics coach who helped her discover her potential in sport.
Since 2011, Suleimon has won more than 20 national medals across sprint events (alongside guide runner Stephen Oyelakin), discus and shot put.
She then began practicing judo and sambo.
"Since I [started] sports I have seen that where there is life, there is hope," she said.
"What sighted people can do, a blind person can do even better.
"I'm proud of myself because it's not easy to be a champion in athletics and in sambo. I don't want to lose the glory."
Her achievements have also become a source of pride for her family. Her twin sister Ganiyat Kehinde Suleimon says her sibling's disability has never defined her worth.
"She is someone we are all proud of. She is now a champion," Ganiyat told BBC Sport Africa.
"Her disability did not make her a liability to us."
For Nigerian sambo coach Olugbenga Adekahunsi, Suleimon's performance in Yerevan offered a glimpse of what she can accomplish with the right support and continued development.
"I see a lot of quality in her because she is very strong and the confidence is there," he told BBC Sport Africa.
"I believe she will become a great sambist."
'No support' for para-athletes
Suleimon says the recognition she has earned internationally has not been matched by adequate "support" at home.
However, her victory is the latest milestone in Nigeria's growing presence in the discipline.
Two years ago Samuel Oladele Kekere became the first blind African to compete at the World Sambo Championships in Kazakhstan, and Sodiq Ajibade followed that with a bronze medal at last year's edition in Kyrgyzstan.
"Despite making Nigeria and the whole of Africa proud, there is nothing to show for it," Suleimon said.
Her concerns reflect wider complaints from Nigerian para-athletes about limited funding, inadequate specialist facilities and insufficient institutional backing, despite their achievements.
Sherif Hammed, vice-president of the Sambo Association of Nigeria, says a lack of resources can prevent talented athletes from reaching their full potential.
"When athletes do not have facilities to train, they cannot compete at the world level," he said.
"It is quite disheartening and heartbreaking.
"People with disabilities, particularly visually impaired athletes, sometimes feel that because of their challenges, they have no purpose in life."
For Suleimon, a Lagos State judo champion, the journey to training is also an issue. Travelling across the city and covering transport costs make maintaining a demanding schedule difficult.
"I leave home at 5.30am to make it to training on time," she explained.
"It takes a lot of money and sacrifice."
Suleimon was unable to follow up her World Cup success at the World Sambo Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, where blind women were again scheduled to compete for the first time.
Beaten in Friday's opening round by Moldova's Ina Cernei, she still hopes her exploits on the global stage can inspire others.
"I want to encourage my fellow blind Africans to believe they can do it," said Suleimon. "And I want to make my country proud again."

What is the average lifespan of recordable Blu-ray discs?
They can last you quite a while, but there are several factors to consider.
At this point, Blu-ray is a niche format, having mostly been supplanted by downloads, streaming and flash storage. But it's easily the format of choice for cinephiles, owing to higher ceilings on picture and audio quality. And if you want to archive files for a long time, Blu-ray may be more affordable, what with flash memory prices spiraling out of control.
How much can you trust recordable Blu-ray discs (BD-R), though? It's not an academic question if the files you're stashing are irreplaceable. If you make a bad decision, you could potentially lose your only digital copies of home videos, say, or a history of all your artistic projects.
Generally speaking, the news here is positive. BD-R may legitimately be your best option. There can be mitigating factors though, such as manufacturing quality, or simply having something to access the content on several years down the road.
How long can recordable Blu-ray discs last?
Short of accidents, the main threat to Blu-ray discs is something called disc rot. This is actually an umbrella term for various forms of decay. The reflective layer can gradually become oxidized, for example. Moisture might attract mold, or cause the layers of a disc to separate. Then there's the matter of exposure to UV (ultraviolet) light, though that's more likely to cause labeling to fade than harm your data. You can potentially notice rot before popping in a disc — look for signs like discoloration or spots.
According to Canadian Conservation Institute data, the cheapest BD-R discs will last five to 10 years on average. These should be avoided for any kind of archival project, since an external SSD is liable to last at least that long, and possibly several times as much while storing a lot more data. Remember, even the biggest BD-R discs top out at 128GB.
That said, manufacturing quality can have a huge impact. In better BD-Rs, a dye recording layer is replaced by a silicon and copper alloy, which you can tell if a disc appears dark gray or grayish-brown. Likewise, these discs might switch to a gold metal layer. The result, the CCI says, is double the lifespan at 10 to 20 years.
It gets better. BD-RE (rewritable) discs can conceivably last you as much as 20 to 50 years. That's so long that you might be able to pass them down to your children or grandchildren. On those timescales, however, other factors should probably discourage you from relying on Blu-ray.
Why BD-R discs might still be a bad idea for long-term storage
The most obvious reason is that discs are fragile. While storage in a relatively dry, dark and cool environment can deter rot, it's all too easy to accidentally crack or scratch a disc in a way that leaves it unreadable. Conversely, many external SSDs use tough metal enclosures that make physical destruction unlikely. All it might take to ruin your disc collection is forgetting that it's at the bottom of a moving box you're hauling, not the top.
Ultimately, the bigger issue might be industry support for Blu-ray. Optical drives have vanished as a default feature on computers, and companies are slowly pulling out the market for both external burners and BD-R discs, even Sony. At the moment, it's not that difficult to find burners and discs if you shop online. But there's no telling whether anyone will still be making this hardware 10 years down the road, much less 20. You could end up with an immaculately-preserved collection and no way of accessing it. Even your current drive might become useless if its software drivers cease to be compatible with later operating systems.
Whatever route you take, it's best not to be completely reliant on one storage medium for critical files. The general rule of thumb these days is to keep one copy in the cloud, and two others on separate forms of local storage. That's not always realistic — at the least, however, you should always be in a position to migrate your files to something fresher.

Madurai Corporation cleared a total of 331 tonnes of garbage, till 6 p.m. on Monday, which was generated across the city on Deepavali day.
Along with the corporation cleanliness workers, volunteers from the Democratic Youth Federation of India, joined the mass cleaning drive early on Monday morning.
Mayor (in-charge), T. Nagarajan, and Corporation Commissioner, Gaurav Kumar, inaugurated the cleanliness drive.
The drive started on the Chithrai Streets, Aavani Moola Streets, Masi Streets, Veli Streets and Vilakkuthoon junction around Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar Temple where commercial establishments, especially textile showrooms, are located.
Besides, the workers focussed on spots at Teppakulam, Mattuthavani bus stand and Vaigai Bank Roads where garbage accumulation is higher.
Besides the usual vehicles used for transporting garbage, 11 earth movers, five bobcat machinery, nine tipper trucks and 42 tractors were involved in the exercise.
The work was expedited in the early hours so much so that 128.40 tonnes of garbage was cleared in the city by 12 noon. This was 33.32 tonnes of additional festival-time garbage removed when compared to 95.08 tonnes cleared during the same time in the last Deepavali season.
The workers had already removed 137 tonnes of garbage on Deepavali day (Sunday).
City Health Officer, Aravind Jothi, Assistant Health Officer, Abishek, DYFI district president, Selva, and secretary, Vel Deva, were present.

WhatsApp Privacy Settings You Should Enable
Hide your Last Seen and Online status
If you care about your privacy and don’t want your people to know when you were online and when you last used the app, WhatsApp allows you to hide the last seen and online status completely
By default, WhatsApp shows the exact time when you last used the app and shows users when you are actually using the app
While these two features let others know when you use WhatsApp, they can also be a downside, especially if others are expecting an immediate reply when they see you online
Fortunately, WhatsApp lets you disable your last seen and completely hide your status. It also gives you more flexibility by letting you hide these from specific contacts, from your contacts, or disable them entirely for everyone.
Here is how to hide your last seen and online status on WhatsApp:
Open WhatsApp on your Android or iPhone and tap the You tab in the bottom-right corner, then tap Privacy.

Hide your profile photo, About, and Links from strangers
Like Last Seen and online status, WhatsApp also shows your profile picture and About to contacts. This also applies to contacts you have outside your network.
Fortunately, like Last Seen and Online Status, WhatsApp also lets you hide your profile photo and About info from strangers, specific contacts, or no one.
How to hide your profile and About from strangers
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture in the bottom right corner of the screen, then tap on Privacy, and then tap on the Profile Picture option
Now you can hide your profile picture, About, and links. To hide it from everyone, set it to Nobody.
If you want to share with all your contacts, select My contacts. To share your profile picture only with specific contacts, tap My contacts except and select the contacts you want to hide your profile picture, About, and links from.
Control who can see and reshare your Status
WhatsApp’s status feature is slowly turning into Instagram Stories. You can now also reshare statuses on WhatsApp. However, unlike Last Seen, this feature is disabled by default.
If you accidentally enabled it and don’t want others to share your status, you can turn off sharing in the status privacy settings. From there, you can also turn off Facebook Stories and Instagram Stories to prevent your WhatsApp status from being shared on other platforms.
How to turn off status sharing on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture, and from here tap on the privacy option
Scroll down, tap Status, then turn off Allow sharing and set your status to be visible only to my contacts. You can also remove specific people by setting up exceptions for contacts, or you can share only with specific contacts. From the bottom, also disable Facebook Stories and Instagram Stories to prevent your status from automatically sharing to Facebook and Instagram Stories.
Turn off read receipts
Even if you hide your online status and last seen on WhatsApp, read receipts can still show blue checkmarks when you read their messages. However, if you don’t want them to know you have read their messages and feel pressured to reply instantly, or if you want better privacy and to balance work and personal WhatsApp chats, you can disable read receipts.
Remember, if you disable it, you also cannot see whether they have read your messages. WhatsApp only shows grey ticks even if you read their messages.
Here is how to turn off read receipts on WhatsApp
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture. Scroll down and tap Privacy. Scroll down again and turn off Read Receipts.
Stop strangers from adding you to groups
Another feature that WhatsApp turns on by default is the ability to let your contacts add you to any groups. This includes the number you have temporarily shared with users you don’t know, and once you add it to the group, your number will be shared with everyone in that group, which is a total privacy nightmare.
Fortunately, WhatsApp allows you to stop random people from adding you to groups.
How to stop people from adding you to random groups
Open WhatsApp and tap on your profile picture, then tap on the privacy option
Scroll down and tap on Groups, then select who can add you to groups. However, WhatsApp doesn’t let you set nobody as an option, but you can still do it by selecting My contacts except and selecting all contacts.
Silence calls from unknown numbers
Since WhatsApp primarily requires your phone number to create an account, once your number is exposed, anyone can contact you on WhatsApp. This is why many of us often receive spam business calls.
However, you can silence unknown calls so that you won’t get notified of random spam calls.
How to silence unknown callers on WhatsApp
To do that, open WhatsApp, tap on your profile picture, and tap on the privacy option
Now scroll down, tap on Calls, and enable the Silence unknown callers option
Make new chats disappear automatically
WhatsApp now supports disappearing messages, which deletes chats from both the sender and receiver after a set time. WhatsApp allows you to enable disappearing messages for individual chats or for the entire WhatsApp for up to 90 days
This is especially useful if you don’t want the other person to save your chats.
Since WhatsApp keeps your messages forever even if you delete your own copy, the other person’s phone still has everything.
When you turn on disappearing messages, WhatsApp also prevents the other person from taking a screenshot and reminds you when they try to save a specific chat.
How to enable disappearing messages on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp, tap your profile picture, then tap Privacy. From here, tap on Default message timer and select how many days you want to set for WhatsApp. You can select up to 90 days or even 24 hours.
If you want to turn on disappearing messages for individual chats, open the new chat and tap on the three-dot menu on the top right corner of the screen, select disappearing messages, and select the timer
Keep WhatsApp photos out of your gallery
By default, WhatsApp saves all photos you receive to your media gallery, including sensitive and personal ones. Even if you lock WhatsApp, anyone can see the photos you received by opening your phone gallery. This also uses your data to automatically download them and increases your storage usage.
WhatsApp allows you to turn off automatic media download and also lets you stop showing media directly from your photos app
How to stop WhatsApp from automatically saving media
First, you can turn off automatic media downloads. To do that, open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner, then scroll down and tap Storage and data.
From there, scroll down and tap Media auto-download, then select all three: when you are using mobile data, when you are connected to Wi-Fi, and when roaming. Then disable all download options, including photos, audio, video, and documents. This prevents files from auto-downloading on Wi-Fi, mobile data, or while roaming.
How to stop WhatsApp from showing media in your device gallery
Open WhatsApp, tap your profile picture, scroll down, tap Chats, then under Chat settings, disable Media visibility.
Turn on two-step verification with a password
WhatsApp also supports two-step verification to prevent your account from getting hacked. While WhatsApp sends a six-digit SMS code for verification, someone with access to that code can log in to your WhatsApp account. However, you can set a second verification method, such as a password, to prevent anyone from accessing your WhatsApp.
Here is how having two-factor authentication adds better security for your WhatsApp account.
Here is how to set two-step verification with a password on WhatsApp
First, open your profile picture in the bottom right corner of the screen, tap on account option, and tap on Password
Now create a new password. Tap Create password and create a new password.
Once you add two-factor authentication, remember to add a recovery email. This is especially useful if you lose your network; your email acts as a secondary verification method, where WhatsApp sends a code to your email instead of sending a verification SMS.
Create a passkey for phishing-proof login
WhatsApp also added support for passkeys; if you’re not sure what a passkey is, we have explained it in a detailed guide.
Passkeys use your fingerprint or Face ID for authentication instead of depending on SMS or passwords. Setting up passkeys lets you log in to your WhatsApp account using your device ID, which is unique to you.
But it also comes with downsides: if someone else has registered a Face ID or fingerprint, they can also log in to your WhatsApp account, so keep note of it.
How to enable passkeys for your WhatsApp account
To enable passkeys, open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner, then tap Account. From here, under the Login and Security section, tap on Passkeys. Then follow the on-screen instructions to create a passkey.
Turn on security notifications
Next, enable security notifications on your WhatsApp account so WhatsApp notifies you if someone switches phones, reinstalls WhatsApp, or changes linked devices. This could also mean someone else accessed their WhatsApp account and signed in on a new device. Turn on security notifications and confirm with the other person why the security key changed.
How to enable security notifications on WhatsApp
To do that, open WhatsApp on your phone. Tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Account. Scroll down, tap Security notifications, and turn on the option that says Show security notifications on this device.
Check linked devices and log out unknown sessions
WhatsApp lets you link and use your account on multiple devices. However, this could also mean someone could link your account to their device without you knowing. So, if you are suspicious about your account activity, you can check linked devices and sign out of any you don’t recognize.
How to check linked devices and log out of unknown devices on your WhatsApp account
Lock WhatsApp with your Biometrics
WhatsApp includes a native app lock feature that lets you lock it with your fingerprint or a pattern. WhatsApp also lets you lock immediately or after a set time. WhatsApp also recently rolled out a new feature to lock WhatsApp Web chats. So, I have made a detailed guide on how to lock WhatsApp on WhatsApp Web. You can watch the video below or follow the detailed steps in this guide.
How to lock your WhatsApp account with your fingerprint or Face ID
Lock and hide your most private chats
WhatsApp also lets you lock individual chats, not just the app. This way, you can lock or hide your most private chats. Here is how.
However, Locked Chat uses your device’s biometrics to lock chats. And if you cannot unlock the chat for any reason, you cannot get those messages back. Your only option is to clear the messages and unlock the chat, which you can do by going to Settings > Privacy, tapping Chat Lock, and tapping Clear Chat Lock. To lock the chats, follow the guide below.
Open WhatsApp on your device and, if you want to lock multiple chats on the home screen, select the chats you want to lock, tap the three-dot menu, and tap Lock chat. You can also do it for individual chats right here only.
Turn on Advanced chat privacy for sensitive chats
While disappearing messages remove your chat after a set period, you can turn on Advanced Chat Privacy for chats with sensitive content. This stops the other user from sharing or exporting your chats, and the media used in the chat won’t be saved in that person’s gallery. It also blocks the new Meta AI used in the chat itself.
Here is how to turn on Advanced Chat Privacy on WhatsApp
Hide your IP address in calls
WhatsApp also supports voice calls. Direct calls can connect your phone to another person’s phone, which can reveal your IP address and, in turn, your location. However, WhatsApp allows you to hide your IP during calls. Here is how.
How to protect your IP address in calls
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Privacy. Then scroll down, tap on Advanced, and enable the option that says ” Protect IP address in calls.
Disable link previews
WhatsApp also supports link previews, which show a preview of the website content. However, to do that, your phone connects to your website and sends a request from your IP address.
So it can easily reveal your phone’s IP address to the website, along with your location. You can also turn off link previews, which prevents those fancy images websites use for spam calls.
How to disable link previews on WhatsApp?
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Scroll down and tap on Privacy. From here, scroll down again, tap Advanced, and enable Disable link previews.
Block floods of messages from unknown accounts
WhatsApp also introduced a new feature that blocks messages from unknown accounts. It blocks unknown accounts that send you high volumes of messages, which is especially useful if you receive frequent spam texts or your WhatsApp is being bombed with multiple messages.
How to block a flood of messages from unknown accounts
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Tap Privacy, then tap Advanced again, and turn on the option that says Block unknown account messages.
Encrypt your chat backup
WhatsApp relies on Google Drive for your WhatsApp backup and iCloud on iPhone. However, by default, your chat backup isn’t encrypted.
You can turn on end-to-end encrypted backup with a passkey, password, or 64-digit key so third-party servers, including Google, can’t read your backup.
Here is how to encrypt your chat backup on WhatsApp
Open WhatsApp and tap your profile picture in the bottom-right corner of the screen, then tap Chats. From here, scroll down and tap Chat backup, then scroll down again and tap End-to-end encrypted backup.
Here, you can turn it on and then use your passkey. Remember, you’ll need this passkey whenever you back up your WhatsApp with this data. You can also use a password or a 64-digit key.
Limit what Meta AI can do with your data
Like any other app, Meta also offers AI features that let you summarise and read messages and also chat with Meta AI. However, because these AI chatbots can’t use your data publicly, Meta uses Private Processing features, which it says process your data privately for those AI features.
However, both of the AI features, including Private Processing features and web search, where Meta AI can search the web based on your queries, are turned off by default. If you turn them on, you can turn them off by default to prevent Meta AI from using your data, even though it is processed privately.
Here is how to turn off the private messaging feature and that switch on WhatsApp
Reserve a username to keep your number private
Recently, WhatsApp introduced usernames on the platform, so instead of your phone number, you can create and share a username and let others contact you through it.
However, your phone number still verifies your account, but for better privacy, you don’t need to reveal it when sharing your WhatsApp account with others. You can also restrict who can message you using your username through a secondary verification method. I have covered in detail how to find your WhatsApp username.
How to reserve a username on WhatsApp?
Use Strict account settings if you’re a high-risk target
If you are a journalist, activist, or public figure, Meta offers Strict Account Settings to help protect your account’s security and privacy. Here is a clear breakdown of the difference between standard settings and Strict Account Settings and how to enable strict account settings for your WhatsApp account.
How to enable Strict Account Settings on WhatsApp?
Run the built-in Privacy Checkup
WhatsApp privacy settings can be confusing for beginners since the platform is used by people of all ages. However, WhatsApp also offers a built-in Privacy Checkup tool that provides a step-by-step process to help you enhance your WhatsApp account’s privacy.
It includes details such as choosing who can contact you, controlling your personal info, the ability to add more privacy to your chats, adding more protection to your account, and much more
This privacy checkup offers detailed, step-by-step instructions to help you enable important privacy settings. If you find any steps in this guide confusing, you can use this tool.
How to access the WhatsApp privacy checkup feature?
