I never liked hunting for Golden Skulltulas in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. The game has 100 of them tucked all over Hyrule, and even over my many hours with the N64 classic growing up, I can’t remember ever actually finding all of them, or even wanting to. Jumping into the Ocarina of Time remake, I expected to ignore the Golden Skulltulas once again. But while poking around Nintendo’s Zelda Notes companion app, I discovered that its maps are a huge help to tracking down all of the elusive golden spiders — and pretty much every other collectible in the game — and now I find myself constantly opening up the app to make sure I haven’t missed a secret.
Ocarina of Time is even better if you use a smartphone app
Finding Ocarina of Time’s hidden collectibles is a lot easier with the help of Zelda Notes.
Inside Zelda Notes, which is available in the free Nintendo Switch app (you don’t need a Switch Online subscription to use it), you can peruse a big map of Hyrule and tap on individual areas for a closer look. The app offers just enough direction to nudge me toward an elusive pickup; when zoomed in, the app drops icons on the map showing you the locations of different collectibles, and if you tap on an icon, the app will show a popup noting any items or special requirements you need to fulfill to be able to obtain it. There are also a bunch of filters you can apply, like swapping between the maps for child and adult Link and toggling categories of icons on and off.
For Skulltula hunting, the map has already saved my sanity many times. While exploring, I’ll often come across the telltale Golden Skulltula sound but have no idea how to get to the tricky spider, even with the help of additional chimes from the new Echo Gem Skulltula tracking item. But with a peek at the Zelda Notes app, I can pinpoint the exact location of where the Skulltula is supposed to be and if I need to use a certain item or change the time of day to be able to get to it.
I recently delved into the Shadow Temple, for example, and I couldn’t figure out how to get up to a Skulltula that I saw while coming down an elevator. But when I checked the icon on the Zelda Notes map, it said that I needed the Scarecrow Song to create a hookshot point, which I hadn’t gotten yet. As soon as I finished the dungeon, getting the Scarecrow Song was my first priority.
Zelda Notes has been useful for tracking down Pieces of Heart, too, which give Link more health once you collect enough. While running up and down Zora’s River, I kept seeing two Pieces of Heart on faraway ledges that I couldn’t figure out how to get to. (My memories of my extensive time with Ocarina of Time as a kid also failed me.) But tapping one of the icons on the Zelda Notes map revealed that I needed a Cucco to get to it — and suddenly, I understood why there was one of the chirping white birds near the entrance of the zone.
Yes, it can be annoying to have to open my phone and dig through an app to track down all of the Skulltulas and other objects of curiosity scattered around Hyrule. I play video games to try and get away from my phone, not look at it more. And sure, I could just look up an online guide, but that often means wading through walkthroughs of varying quality, trusting an AI summary, or scrubbing through a YouTube video. But with Zelda Notes, I’m usually in and out relatively quickly, putting down my phone after seeing a clue or an icon that pushes me in the direction of the next golden spider. I’ve already found more than 70 Golden Skulltulas, and to my surprise, I now want to hunt for the full 100.

Meta Platforms said on Monday it would expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults, as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
Teen Accounts, available on Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, include built-in protections that automatically limit who can contact teens, the content they see and their time on the apps.
Parents in the US will begin receiving Instagram notifications this month explaining how teens are placed in age-appropriate protections, Meta said.
In Australia, Meta has begun using Apple’s age-range signal as an additional method to help determine users’ ages.
Meta said it is continuing to roll out the technology on Facebook and will begin launching similar technology globally on Threads later this year.
Meta faces multiple lawsuits over allegations that its platforms harm teens.
In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every US state and territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms’ harm to teens.
Under the settlements, Meta agreed to improve how it identifies teens and children under 13.
Meta settled with a teen plaintiff last month in a Los Angeles trial testing claims that Instagram and Facebook were designed to be addictive, causing mental health problems and an eating disorder.

I return to my room as my mother-in-law leaves for her office in the building adjacent to our home. I am about to start my bath when I hear a series of explosions, as of firecrackers, but different. I freeze. Someone comes pounding frantically on my bathroom door. It is Ongmu, the children’s nanny, crying hysterically. I fling open the door, my heart thumping. She is gesticulating wildly, speechlessly, towards the garden.
I run along the path leading to Akbar Road. I see the white Ambassador car slowly moving towards the same path. I hesitate. I stop, heart in my mouth. Dread, panic, fear. I feel suffocated. I can’t breathe. I am about to collapse. No, no, I can’t. I have to walk to the car. I see her being carried into it. I understand; I scream.
I’m in the car now, crouching on the floor, facing her … Blood – blood on her sari, blood on her chest. Her large eyes are wide open; her face wears a surprised expression. She doesn’t move. I attempt to speak to her, to call out, “Mummy, Mummy”, but no word comes out. I try again; she doesn’t reply.
Her aides are in the front of the car, screaming. Heavy, slow traffic, the car barely moves, it has no siren. One red light, then another. Then the hospital. The gate isn’t opening. Chaos. We are stopped; someone looks through the window in a questioning attitude. They let us in.
We reach the emergency department, teeming with people. We are stopped again, not allowed in, we have to wait for our turn. Someone calls out to the driver, signals him to move forward. They identify us; she is placed on a trolley. We are led somewhere – an operation theatre? They ask me to follow. I’m taken to a room nearby. No, no, I want to stay by her, I insist. I want to know. I have to see. They don’t reply; they are immersed in their emergency procedures.
I feel confused, lost … I don’t recognise anyone there. I’m shivering under my dressing gown. I feel scared, my mind is racing. Where is Rajiv? I try to remember. I can’t, I can’t. The children, yes, they’re in school; they must be brought home. Oh God, no, no. Let them be safe, let Rajiv be safe … Whom do I tell, whom do I speak to? I sense someone in the room. I don’t know who it is. I try to speak, to put some words together; nothing comes out. “There’s blood all over her clothes,” someone says. Some clothes are brought in for me. I am helped into them in a nearby closet.
Hours go by, agonising hours. More people come in and crowd around. I signal a question to the doctor; he shakes his head. I understand, yes, I understand. I break into sobs, uncontrollably. Someone tries to calm me. I feel numb, cold.
At two in the afternoon of 31 October 1984, Indira Gandhi was declared dead. I was driven home to collect some clothes for her body to be changed into. On the way, a group of men tried to stop our car, banging on its windows. They were angry, shouting something I couldn’t understand.
At home, the children, Rahul and Priyanka, rushed to my arms in tears. When they had been abruptly picked up from school by black-uniformed commandos, they sensed a catastrophe. Once home, they saw some of the staff sobbing. They asked question after question. “Where’s Mama?” “Why have we been brought home?” “Where’s Papa?” “What’s happened?” “Where’s Dadi?” “You aren’t telling us the truth!” My friends Nina and Sterre had been with them, trying to calm them down, not knowing what to say to them. I wanted to sit with them and hug them, to break the news to them gently, but I was unable to – I had to go back; Rajiv was coming to the hospital.
Rajiv had been in West Bengal at a political rally when his cavalcade was stopped by a police patrol. He was told there was a message from Delhi to say he should rush back – a serious accident had taken place. He was driven to the helipad, from where he flew to Calcutta and then to Delhi. He’d heard on a BBC bulletin that Mrs Gandhi was wounded and in a grave condition. Nobody told him directly that his mother was no more, but he understood.
He landed at 3.30pm and was driven straight to the hospital. He walked in with other people, and I remember longing to be left alone with him for a moment at least. We held each other, and as he spoke to me, it sunk in that he was saying something I didn’t want to hear. “I have been asked … They want me to be sworn in as prime minister.”
I felt as if a knife had been plunged right into my heart. I felt a pounding in my chest, a rage welling up deep inside me. I was about to explode. I attempted to hold it in. “You have been asked to? How dare they ask? How dare they? Who are they? Why you, why does it have to be you? Why did you allow them to ask you? No, it cannot be; this time it’s not going to be!” Seized by utter pain and anguish, soaked in perspiration, I felt like throwing up. I wanted to scream, to ask for help. “Someone please help me put an end to this.”
I burst out crying, pleading, begging him with folded hands, “No, no, you can’t think of it. You have to stop them, you must refuse, you must say no – for the children’s sake, for yourself. You can’t do this to us. They will kill you; they will kill you, too!” I cried out. He replied, “They will kill me anyway.”
We brought my mother-in-law home. The dining room had been emptied out, and we laid her body down on the floor, her feet pointing south as Hindu custom decrees. The same evening at around 6.30pm, Rajiv was sworn in as prime minister of India. I was too broken to even register what was happening around me. His mother lay there, her body pierced with more than 30 bullet holes. I knew, I knew it then in my heart: Rajiv’s path would lead to the same end.

Three social media content creators from West Bengal — Akash Sarkar, Surajit Shee and Srimoyee Chakraborty — were recently arrested after making posts which questioned the ruling BJP government and its policies.
While Sarkar was granted bail on October 29 after spending three days in police custody, Chatterjee was released from detention on a personal bond on October 26. Shee was first sent to judicial custody and held at Medinipur Central Jail. At present, he is in police custody till November 6.
An FIR was lodged against Shee under Sections 152, 197 and 353 of the BNS, pertaining to acts endangering integrity of India, assertions threatening national integration, and statements amounting to public mischief, respectively.
In the FIR registered against Sarkar, the police invoked Sections 356(1), 353(1)(2) and 299(1) of the BNS, pertaining to criminal defamation, spreading false information/hate speech, and intentionally outraging religious feelings, respectively.
Surajit Shee: Posts on Durga Puja Stampede
Surajit Shee, hailing from Dantan village of West Midnapore district, runs a Facebook page called ‘Core Bangla-Janakantha’, which has over 2,52,000 followers. Shee shares posts on a range of social, political and scientific issues. The two last posts on his page were made on October 19. In one, he is seen appreciating the BJP government for banning DJs and loudspeakers during processions in the state, and in the other post, he talks about allegations that followed the Chorbagan stampede which killed 19 people in Kolkata at a Durga Puja.
Another post by Shee from October 18 caried a video that has been restricted in India. The caption reads, translated from Bengali, “What is the actual truth behind the Chorebagan incident? Which version is correct? The official government figures or the claims made by the public? The government itself is abusing the law. Those in power are misusing their authority to silence the voices of ordinary citizens.”
Shee is a member of ‘Bharatiya Biggyan o Juktibadi Samity’ — an organization which aims to promote scientific temperament in the society.
Alt News spoke with Dipak Roy, a key member of the outfit. Roy mentioned that beside discussing political issues, Shee was vocal about various scientific and social issues.
“Surajit had been telling us that for almost a year that a section of local BJP-RSS workers had been harassing him over his social media content. The intensity of the harassment increased after May 4 (as BJP came to power in the state). On either October 17 or 18, Shee told me that his house had been attacked by the same group, who claimed that he was posting anti-national content. I suggested that he take shelter elsewhere. He then went to a friend’s house in Contai. The police arrested him from there on October 24,” alleged Roy.
Although Shee was detained by police on October 24, he was shown as arrested on October 25, Sunday, from his residence in Dantan, instead of Contai.
According to Roy, the group that attacked Shee’s house claimed that a complaint had been lodged against him at Dantan police station over his alleged ‘anti-national’ activities. Roy told Alt News that when Shee’s father and father-in-law went to the police station to enquire about the alleged complaints, the police could not produce any complaint lodged against him. Police allegedly told them that the chief minister had ordered Shee’s arrest and that it “would be better if he surrendered” or else they would “make an example out of him”.
During the arrest, Roy alleged that only three to four police personnel were present while nearly 20 RSS-BJP workers rounded him up. “Around 15-20 RSS-BJP workers surrounded the house of his friend in Contai. These people assaulted him before handing him over to the police, who then took him away in a car,” alleged Roy. “We thought Contai police had arrested him and arranged for a lawyer to represent him at the Contai sub-divisional court. However, later we realised that Shee had been arrested by Dantan police and was produced before the Dantan court.”
Roy further alleged that Shee’s family could access the legal documents related to the case two days after his arrest. Police have also allegedly seized Shee’s mobile phone, but no seizure list has been provided to his family.
Alt News’ attempts to contact both Dantan and Contain police were unsuccessful till publication time.
Alt News spoke to Tapan Jana, Shee’s maternal uncle, who said, “Surajit was produced in Dantan court on November 2, and police sought seven days of custody. However, the judge allowed only four days.”
“After he was remanded to police custody, an officer from Dantan police station verbally abused us when we went to meet him. The officer said that Surajit had insulted Sanatan Dharma, the state and central governments, and was inciting the public through his Facebook posts. He told us to make sure that Surajit reveals during questioning who had instructed him to make those posts,” Jana said.
“The officer further said that unless Shee confessed, he would make it difficult for him to get bail,” Jana added.
Akash Sarkar: Posts on Stampede and Suvendu Adhikari
Akash Sarkar (30) was arrested from his home in Nagerbazar on October 25, produced before the Barrackpore court on October 26, which ordered three days of police custody. He was released on bail on October 29.
Sarkar told Alt News that during interrogation, police pointed to three aspects of his posts which they claimed led to his arrest — his reference to Suvendu Adhikari’s ‘bhaipo’ (nephew) in connection with the Chorbagan stampede, his comments about the government’s handling of the situation following the stampede, and his use of the term ‘teen bati’ (three bowls) to refer to Adhikari.
Sarkar said, “In one of my Facebook posts, I had mentioned that Suvendu’s nephew was the chief patron of Chorbagan Sarbojonin, the puja where 19 people were trampled, and that he should take responsibility for the tragedy. I had also flagged the manner in which the Durga idol, with its hands tied, was taken away by the police for immersion.”
“I had written in my Facebook post that, according to the BJP, previous governments in West Bengal were not Sanatani. But even those governments did not treat the goddess in the way the Sanatani government treated her. The police flagged my post as religiously inflammatory and kept me in custody for three days,” added Sarkar.
According to Sarkar, in another post, he had addressed chief minister as ‘teen bati’ — a political jab aimed at Adhikari.
“The ‘teen bati’ jab was popularised by Ali Aftab Chand, a lawyer at the Calcutta high court who identifies himself as a ‘Rashtravadi Muslim’. He was not arrested. Is it because he is close to the BJP?” asked Sarkar.
According to the FIR, a person named Soumen Das had lodged a complaint against Sarkar, alleging that Sarkar “has been using his Facebook profile to publish false, defamatory, religiously inflammatory and provocative posts concerning the Hon’ble Prime Minister of India, Sri Narendra Modi and Hon’ble Chief Minister of India, Sri Suvendu Adhikari.”
“While I was in the lock-up, I heard from a few police personnel that our local MLA, Tarunjyoti Tiwari, had visited the police station and taken a personal interest in my case. Police hinted that although the charges against me were flimsy, orders from higher-ups were forcing them to keep me in custody,” he alleged, adding that the police was yet to return his phone.
Srimoyee Chakroborty: Posts Critical of State Government
Chakraborty had posted an update on her Facebook profile on October 26, mentioning that she had been held at the Bidhannagar East police station. She was later released the same day on a bond of Rs 2,000.
On October 26, she announced on Facebook that she was detained, while vowing to continue her fight. Her posts on Facebook reflect a similar pattern of posts critical of the BJP-led state and central government and its policies. However, it is not clear which particular post led to the administrative action.
A scroll through her Facebook timeline shows her vocal support for the Left.
Similar to Shee and Sarkar, Chakraborty had also made a series of posts critical of the government’s management of the Chorbagan stampede and the immersion process. On October 21, she shared the chief minister’s video where he announced that only people who follow Sanatana Dharma would participate in the Durga idol immersion process. In the caption, she referred to Adhikari as ‘teen bati’.

On today’s episode of Variety‘s “Strictly Business” podcast, movie marketing veteran Gerry Rich details his new memoir “Chasing Hollywood: A Marketing Chief’s Lessons on Breaking Through.”
Rich has worked for most of Hollywood’s major studios, including Paramount, Columbia Pictures, MGM, Miramax and Amazon MGM Studios. He looks back at moments of triumph such as the 2008 opening of “Iron Man,” which launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe. And Rich looks ahead to how the discipline of entertainment marketing and audience targeting is changing in the age of AI.
“Going back even a decade or two we had the ability to reach a broad audience all at one time. Through linear television and cable and sports and digital and social media, we were able to hit a broad swath of the audience in real time,” Rich says. “It’s much more difficult to do that now, particularly with linear TV. The only thing that really gets a significant audience is would be live sports, particularly football. That’s where we’re assured of getting a captive audience, a broad audience, a significant audience all at once. All of that has changed quite a bit.”
Rich recalls the heady experience of building buzz for the “Iron Man” release in 2008, when the industry was skeptical about the market for elevated superhero movie. And star Robert Downey Jr. had a lot to prove after public battles with personal demons that inevitably hurt his star power.
“ Iron Man didn’t have the notoriety as IP as Spider-Man or X-Men or any of the better known characters. So there was some uncertainty as to whether or not Iron Man would be able to resonate for the broadest audience and deliver superhero-type grosses. There was also a lot of skepticism about whether Robert Downey Jr. was the right guy to play this character, this flawed character. And there was a lot of questions as to whether or not [director] Jon Favreau could deliver a movie with the adequate and necessary scope and scale,” Rich recalls.
“But we really felt and as soon as we saw dailies that there was something really extraordinary happening with that movie. And what we decided to do was hold off showing any assets from the film until Comic-Con of 2007, well before the release of the movie,” he says. “And that’s when we brought the entire crew down [to Comic-Con]. Jon Favreau came out to a thunderous applause. And he had his iPhone, capturing the response of the audience and he just had the group from the very beginning. We showed the teaser trailer that we were going to launch, as well as some film footage, and the audience was sold. They came out as major champions of the film.”

United Nations peacekeepers and South Sudanese authorities failed to take adequate action despite warnings weeks before insurgents raided a village and killed more than 200 people earlier this year, Amnesty International said in a report released on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
The rights group said that the peacekeeping mission, known by the acronym UNMISS, knew that an attack on Abiemnom, a remote area near the border with Sudan, was likely but failed to reinforce the roughly three dozen peacekeepers based there until after it occurred.
Between 1,000 and 1,500 armed men from neighbouring Mayom County carried out the March 1 attack, shooting residents, burning homes and looting part of the hospital, Amnesty said.
The death toll was at least 213, according to authorities, including 130 town residents, 76 security personnel and seven foreign nationals.
“Both the government and UNMISS had sufficient information and time to take more effective preventive action. Their failure to take stronger action cost lives,” said Tigere Chagutah, an Amnesty regional director.
UNMISS spokesperson Priyanka Chowdhury said in a statement that the mission did its best with limited resources to provide protection and medical care to roughly 2,500 people who sheltered at a protected area established in anticipation of the attack.
Facing budget cuts and reduced personnel, she said that the mission "concentrated its available capacity on immediate protection of civilians seeking refuge within our base rather than dispersing limited forces across tasks they could not safely sustain simultaneously.”
The March assault came amid renewed fighting between government forces and an array of opposition groups, undermining a 2018 agreement that ended five years of civil war. The area has experienced cycles of retaliatory violence linked to land access and cattle raiding.
Amnesty said that the March attack may have been triggered by unresolved killings of several young men from neighbouring Mayom County in Abiemnom.
The investigation drew on interviews with 82 people, including survivors, witnesses and medical workers, along with satellite imagery and verified photographs and videos.
Survivors described residents being shot in their homes or while trying to flee. Some were killed at close range after being captured or wounded, Amnesty said. Government security forces and armed residents tried to repel the attackers but were overwhelmed.
One mother of seven told researchers that attackers shot her daughter-in-law as she held her youngest child. Amnesty withheld interviewees' real names to protect them.
Satellite imagery showed more than 230 structures destroyed by fire. Most victims were buried in two mass graves, according to the report.
Ms. Chowdhury acknowledged that UNMISS was aware tensions had been high since mid-February and that people sought protection at its base in the days leading up to the attack.
She said that UNMISS repeatedly asked the national army to deploy additional security forces to the area after receiving early warnings of an attack.
The mission sent 40 additional police personnel afterwards. Amnesty questioned why those reinforcements hadn't been deployed earlier, particularly after a similar deadly attack in April 2025.
Ms. Chowdhury's statement didn't explicitly address why the reinforcements were sent after the attack rather than before.
South Sudanese authorities didn't respond to two letters seeking information and comment on the findings, Amnesty said. Government spokesperson Ateny Wek Ateny also didn't respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press.
The group called for an independent investigation into the killings and a separate review of the peacekeepers’ response, with both sets of findings made public.
Protecting civilians is a central task of UNMISS. The UN Security Council renewed its mandate in April while reducing its authorised troop ceiling from 17,000 to 12,000.

England Women’s tour of West Indies has lost its much-awaited Test match, with the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) revising its April schedule to make room for a more extensive red-ball programme ahead of the Women’s Ashes.
The tour will now consist of three T20Is and three ODIs. The ECB said there was insufficient time to fit in the Test originally anticipated, because the trip takes place once the English domestic season is already under way.
The change allows England to play four red-ball matches in home conditions before the Ashes Test against Australia at Headingley, which starts on June 24. They include a three-day fixture against Australia A and three best v best matches on English soil. At least two of the intra-squad games will let selectors look at a wider pool of players in the format.
The programme begins in January with a 10-day red-ball training camp in Bengaluru, ahead of the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy.
The ECB said the current domestic structure offers few chances for players to experience multi-day cricket, so management looked for the best way to prepare the team for four days of cricket against Australia.
Dates and venues for the West Indies tour will be confirmed by Cricket West Indies in due course. It will follow the opening round of One-Day Cup matches, which will involve all England players. The ECB thanked Cricket West Indies for agreeing to its request and for its “understanding and collaborative approach”.
ECB Chief Executive Richard Gould said the Headingley Test would be “one of the highlights of the summer” and is worth four points in the multi-format series, making preparation vital.
“A 10-day warm-weather red-ball camp in India followed by four further matches in English conditions will provide Charlotte Edwards and her team with the appropriate game time to be ready for that challenge,” he said.
Gould added that best v best cricket in English conditions would help the ECB gauge its strength in depth and give more players competitive multi-day experience. “We appreciate the constructive conversations with Cricket West Indies,” he said, “that have enabled us to look forward to an exciting tour of the Caribbean before focusing our attentions back on our home summer.”

Headquarters of Haitian gang destroyed, El Salvador's president says
- Published
The headquarters of one of Haiti's largest crime gangs has been destroyed by El Salvador's military, the Salvadoran president has said.
The infamous 400 Mawozo gang, which is known for kidnappings and intimidation tactics, was targeted in a ground and air attack at a complex on the outskirts of Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince.
It is El Salvador's first military action on a Haitian target since it deployed more than 2,000 soldiers there last month, as part of a mission to rescue four missing Salvadoran technicians.
Haiti has been plagued by gang violence for years, with heavily armed groups controlling large parts of the capital, and beyond.
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele announced the news on X, external, boasting that most of the gang members fled without trying to fight.
"We destroyed the house of [gang leader] Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters," he wrote on Tuesday.
The post was accompanied by video of several helicopters firing on a large complex, reportedly in the suburb of Croix-des-Bouquets, the gang's stronghold.
As the helicopters circle above, dozens of people can be seen running out of the property, fleeing the strikes.
Several media outlets have reported that as many as 20 people were killed, however that has not been confirmed by authorities. There has also been no official confirmation of the extent of the damage at the property, with Haitians questioning whether it has been destroyed or just damaged.
The Miami Herald reports that the gang's leader, Wilson "Lanmò San Jou" Joseph, was not there at the time.
The BBC has not been able to verify the video posted by Bukele, nor whether the property is indeed the gang's headquarters.
Haiti's National Police drone task force was involved in the attack, supported by Salvadoran soldiers, the Miami Herald reports, citing several sources.
Posting on X after the strikes, Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé thanked the Salvadoran military's commitment "in the fight against gangs", and said the two nations would keep working together, along with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF), to "regain control of the territory and restore state authority".
"THE GANGS WILL GET NO SLEEP!" he added.
Some 2,000 Salvadoran soldiers were deployed to Haiti last month after four air force technicians were abducted at gunpoint while food shopping in October.
El Salvador's right-wing president has vowed to bring the men home alive and warned the gang to release them immediately or face sustained pressure from his military.
The four abducted men were working as part of the GSF, made up of troops from several nations, initially led by soldiers from Chad.
President Bukele's move to send thousands of Salvadoran troops to Haiti has raised concerns, with critics saying they are not all working within the command structure of the GSF. It has raised questions about the operational legitimacy and legality of their actions in the Caribbean nation.
Amnesty International has urged both countries to "ensure all operations conducted by Salvadoran forces in Haiti comply with international human rights law".
Such concerns do not appear to faze Bukele, however, who continues to directly warn and target the gang leaders.
The attack on the supposed gang headquarters seemingly came after a user on X had urged Bukele to attack the complex.
"Where is that house? Give us the exact address, and we'll destroy it," he replied to the post, which has now been taken down, apparently for violating X's rules.
The 400 Mawozo gang is the largest criminal organisation in Haiti, and known for kidnappings, extortion, murders and arms trafficking.
Haiti is the poorest country in the Americas and remains largely under gang control.
At least 5,700 people have been killed or injured there by gangs or during operations against them between 1 January and 11 September this year alone, the United Nations has said.
El Salvador has recorded huge reductions in gang violence under President Bukele as part of a sweeping crackdown, and he has vowed to do the same in Haiti.
However, human rights groups have argued that the way he has done it is unlawful, with the open-ended extension of emergency laws, the treatment of detainees in El Salvador's high-security mega-prison and the mass trials of alleged gang members.

Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20.
On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum’s closure:
The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.
You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site.
We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.
For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied.
Apple reportedly told MacRumors that it is shutting down the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs.
The Apple Support Community dates to 1998, when the online forum was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Two years later, Apple renamed the community forum to Apple Discussions. In 2011, Apple revamped the forum, adding dedicated communities for specific devices and the ability to track responses to posted questions, while renaming it Apple Support Communities. By 2022, the forum was called Apple Support Community, as MacRumors noted this week.
Based on yesterday’s announcement, it seems Apple now prefers that its customers rely on official Apple employees for technical support. The forum may also have become less popular as rival forums grow, including Reddit and the technical support communities on the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums.

Kenya discharges last Ebola patient, beginning countdown to Ebola-free declaration
Kenya has discharged its last Ebola patient, starting a 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free
NAIROBI, Kenya -- Kenya on Wednesday discharged its last Ebola patient, officially beginning the 42-day countdown toward being declared Ebola-free, even as the number of cases recorded in the wider region topped 11,000 since the outbreak began in May.
The country recorded nine Ebola cases in October after the first patient traveled from Congo through Uganda, transmitting the virus to four family members and four healthcare workers.
The first patient and his mother died of Ebola, while the other seven patients have fully recovered. The government had identified 135 contacts who had interacted with the first patient.
Kenya now begins the 42-day countdown to being declared Ebola-free, provided no new infections are recorded during that period.
But while Kenya's cases have now been discharged, elsewhere in the region the number of infections continues to climb. In Congo, the epicenter of the outbreak, 11,042 people have been infected and 5,387 have died, the government said Wednesday.
The outbreak also spread to Uganda and Nigeria through individuals who traveled from Congo.
Kenya's Health Minister Aden Duale on Wednesday said the 42-day waiting period is twice the longest Ebola incubation period and would end on Dec. 23, but insisted that the country would continue with its prevention measures.
The Ministry of Health had earlier expressed confidence that the outbreak was under control, noting that all confirmed cases were linked to the first patient’s contact list. This indicated that there had been no community transmission.
Kenya has faced travel restrictions following the Ebola outbreak, with Saudi Arabia announcing an indefinite suspension of visas on Oct. 30. The decision affected hundreds of Kenyan workers traveling to the Gulf for employment, particularly as domestic and hotel workers.
The Ministry of Health had urged Saudi Arabia to reconsider the travel restrictions, explaining that Kenya’s first Ebola case was imported and that all subsequent cases were traced to the initial patient’s contact list. The ministry said all contacts had been identified and traced in line with established outbreak-control guidelines.
The current Ebola outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the virus and has been described as one of the worst outbreaks on record.
Kenya tightened its border controls designating a specific gate at the country's main airport for passengers traveling from 10 countries that have reported Ebola cases or border those that have active cases. Passengers are being screened using thermal technology and all new arrivals fill a health declaration form that provides their travel and health information.

Australia considers criminal penalties for rogue AI in wake of OpenAI hack
- Published
Australia plans to create a new AI safety regulator and has flagged criminal penalties for tech companies who do not comply, months after an OpenAI hack.
In September, Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that a rogue OpenAI agent had "infiltrated" a government health website and other systems, and criticised the company for taking months to tell them about the hack.
On Tuesday, he released the 18 recommendations made after a "rapid review" into the breaches including new safety and security standards for AI companies such as mandatory reporting of hacks.
AI brings opportunities, he said, but Australia must prepare for the "new risks" from this "rapidly advancing technology".
"The law needs to get ahead of and, in some cases, make sure that it catches up with, what is a very fast changing world," Albanese said.
One of the recommendations suggests changes to criminal law to have a standalone "failure to prevent" offence .
This would criminalise instances where a company develops "an AI model that engages in harmful conduct" and "fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm".
The review also recommended "mandatory, time-bound AI safety reporting" of hacks.
This point addresses what Albanese had earlier called his "disappointment" in the months-long delay for OpenAI to tell his government about the breach.
In June, a statistics portal containing "non-sensitive" data from Australia's universal healthcare scheme Medicare was hacked by a rogue OpenAI agent.
OpenAI said it only learnt of the breach in August while reviewing "misaligned model activity" and emailed a general inbox of an Australian government agency on 10 September.
It took several more days before the email was escalated to Australia's cybersecurity centre, with a message then sent to a government minister ahead of the prime minister being told.
Albanese said he spoke to OpenAI boss Sam Altman and raised "Australia's extreme concern about this incident", with Altman acknowledging there were "issues with protocols" at OpenAI.
Days after the hacks were revealed, OpenAI delayed its rollout of a new AI model, citing safety concerns.

Austria tightens laws against spying to protect the international organizations it hosts
Austria has launched plans to tighten its espionage laws, which currently only ban spying against Austria itself
BERLIN -- Austria's government on Wednesday launched plans to tighten the country's laws against spying, which at present explicitly ban espionage directed against Austria itself but not if it targets other countries or international organizations.
Austria is a European Union member that has a policy of military neutrality dating back to the 1950s. Its capital, Vienna, is host to several U.N. agencies including the International Atomic Energy Agency. It is also the home of other international groups such as the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe and the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, or OPEC.
“Espionage is a real threat to our security, to security in our country, but above all to our reputation as Austria, as the capital of dialogue, as an official location of the U.N. and over 40 international organizations,” Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger said as Cabinet ministers presented the draft legislation. “We have a responsibility ... and we are fulfilling this responsibility.”
Meinl-Reisinger acknowledged that Vienna has often been described as a “capital of espionage,” a reputation dating back to the Cold War, but said she wants to dispense with any “romantic idea” of spying.
She said that “we are responding to the current hybrid threat situation.” That's a term for non-conventional hostile acts such as sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and an array of other methods.
Austria’s criminal code currently states that anyone who “sets up or operates a secret intelligence service to the detriment of the Republic of Austria or supports such an intelligence service in whatever way” faces a prison sentence of up to five years. It also bans setting up, operating or supporting a “military intelligence service” for a foreign power.
The new legislation, which requires parliamentary approval, will increase the maximum sentence for espionage to the detriment of Austria to 10 years, Meinl-Reisinger said. It will explicitly criminalize spying against international organizations or the EU, with a maximum sentence of five years.
Officials said that the legislation also will explicitly ban recruiting agents and being recruited as an agent, among other things. That's a measure targeted in particular at the recruitment of so-called “throwaway agents,” people recruited for low-level espionage actions without necessarily knowing what they are getting into.
The justice minister in Austria's last government announced a similar plan in 2024 but that administration didn't agree on legislation before that year's election.
Meinl-Reisinger said that “we are no longer looking away.” She said that entry visas for diplomats have been denied in 63 cases since she took office in March 2025, and noted that eight Russian diplomats have been expelled from Austria in that time.

Police said the elderly man allegedly took advantage of the family's absence and sexually assaulted the child. He allegedly inflicted serious injuries on her private parts.
A 70-year-old man was arrested in Gujarat's Surat after allegedly molesting his three-year-old granddaughter and inflicting serious injuries on her while other family members were away from home, police said.
The incident took place in the Dindoli police station area on November 8. According to the complaint filed by the child's mother, the family had gone to clean their new house at around 3 pm during the Diwali holidays. As the three-year-old girl was sleeping at home, she was left in the care of her maternal grandfather.
Police said the elderly man allegedly took advantage of the family's absence and sexually assaulted the child. He allegedly inflicted serious injuries on her private parts.
When the family returned home in the evening, they found the child bleeding profusely. On being questioned by her parents, the girl began crying and communicated through gestures what had happened to her.
The family subsequently questioned the grandfather, who allegedly confessed to the act, according to the complaint.
Following the incident, the child's family approached the Dindoli police station and lodged a written complaint against the 70-year-old man. Based on the complaint, police registered a case under the relevant sections and arrested the accused.
Further legal proceedings and an investigation into the incident are underway.

Nabu Casa — the commercial side of the Open Home Foundation, which runs Home Assistant — just launched the Home Assistant Connect Aux-2, a multi-function box designed to help you bring more non-smart devices into your smart home. It’s part of Home Assistant’s ongoing efforts to become more user-friendly. And it’s working.
Hands on with Home Assistant’s new ‘smart home multi-tool’
The Home Assistant Connect Aux-2 helped me track my fridge temperature and finally set up my in-wall speakers.
If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
I’ve been testing the Aux-2 for a couple days and I’ve found it unsurprisingly useful and surprisingly easy to set up. The Aux-2 is a $69 box about the size of a deck of cards. It has 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, USB-A, USB-C, a digital/analog audio jack, a Grove port for interfacing with peripherals like sensors, buttons, and LEDs, and a pair of RS-232 serial ports.
It can bridge Bluetooth devices into your Home Assistant setup. Its USB port lets you plug in a Nabu Casa Z-Wave or Zigbee antenna in case your Home Assistant hub isn’t in a good spot. You can control devices like TVs, AV receivers, solar inverters, and more via serial connector. And you can connect an amplifier or powered speakers to its audio jack to stream music to older audio equipment.
All of these things leverage Home Assistant’s capabilities as an open-source platform. The Aux-2 is based on ESPHome, an open platform for making DIY smart home devices from cheap, flexible ESP boards, and it uses existing Home Assistant/ESPHome integrations for all its features. The serial integration was developed earlier this year; Music Assistant and SendSpin, which power the audio-out feature, are in active development.
I have a Home Assistant install, but even after several years it is not my primary smart home platform simply because of friction and time constraints. Instead, I have a hodgepodge of Google Home, Apple Home, and a few devices that are only in Home Assistant. The situation is not ideal.
But the Aux-2’s capabilities perfectly intersect with two things I’d been meaning to do anyway, one of which I’m already using Home Assistant for. First, I have a garage fridge, because I live in Texas. I also have children, which means sometimes the fridge or freezer door gets left open. I want to know when that happens before all my food goes bad.
A couple years ago, I set up a few Aqara temperature sensors, connected to Home Assistant via a now-discontinued Zigbee dongle, and set up an automation to alert me if the fridge or freezer get too warm. But they frequently drop connection (probably because they’re inside a fridge in the garage), they chew through coin cell batteries, and they have no displays, which means I also have a cheap Acu-rite hygrometer in the fridge so I can see the temperature without pulling out my phone. Someone tipped me off to Govee’s Bluetooth hygrometers, but I’d need a Bluetooth proxy to get them into Home Assistant. That happens to be a feature of the Aux-2.
I also have a set of in-wall speakers in my living room that I’ve never used. I’d been meaning to get an amp, but analysis paralysis set in. Do I get a Wiim Amp? A stereo receiver? A cheap Bluetooth amp? Do I try to get them to work with my four Sonos speakers? Maybe my ancient Google Home speaker? Turns out I do nothing for five years. Maybe the Aux-2 could help.
Setting up the Aux-2 was much easier than I expected. I plugged it into my computer via USB-C and was able to download and install the latest firmware right from a browser. I could also add my Wi-Fi credentials. Then I unplugged it, moved it over to my media console and connected it to power (it takes USB-C or power over Ethernet), and did the rest of the setup in the Home Assistant interface.
In HA, I was prompted to install ESPHome, which discovered the Aux-2 and sent me to a “set up your ESPHome device page” that walked me through the capabilities. Enabling Bluetooth proxying took a couple of clicks; I added the Govee Bluetooth integration and put batteries into the sensors and they showed up automatically. Mercifully, they maintained their Bluetooth connection through three walls and a fridge, and now my fridge monitoring setup works again.
The audio capability took a little longer, but most of that was spent hooking the speakers up to the amp I ended up buying and setting up Music Assistant, which I didn’t have installed. Music Assistant lives on your Home Assistant hardware and can play from many different services — from Spotify to YouTube Music to local files and more — and to many different outputs, like Sonos, Wiim, AirPlay, Google Cast, and others, but they all need to be configured, and that took a beat. Not a long beat: less than half an hour total.
I can now play music to the in-wall speakers using Music Assistant. Sendspin, the whole-home audio standard (also developed by the Open Home Foundation) is supposed to be able to let you group speakers from different protocols under certain conditions, but I haven’t gotten that working yet. The standard is still in development, and I’ve also been busy, so I’m not sure if that’s a me problem or a them problem.
I would also like to see the Aux-2 show up as an AirPlay or Spotify Connect target, which (again) is probably just a thing I need to set up.
Serial control is the most intriguing feature of the Aux-2, and it’s unfortunately the thing I haven’t yet had time to test. But the ability to hook in things like solar inverters, TVs, and receivers is fascinating and one I want to look into further when I get the chance. Maybe I’ll hook it up to my LG TV.
The Aux-2 doesn’t do anything you couldn’t do already with an ESP32 board and various accessories, or even other ESP-based devices. The Apollo Automations Cast-1, for example, costs $35 and supports the same music-casting and Bluetooth proxy features I’m actually using from the Aux-2 at the moment. You could bodge together something even cheaper with DIY parts.
That’s not a knock against the Aux-2. That’s the whole point. The ecosystem is open by design, which I find endlessly refreshing. Both Nabu Casa and Apollo fund the Open Home Foundation, which develops Home Assistant and ESPHome (and Sendspin and Music Assistant), and both provide hardware that’s a little easier to use than DIY options. But there’s nothing stopping you from making your own devices. It’s actively encouraged.
I bought a three-pack of ESP32 boards for $16 three years ago. I could have built a Bluetooth proxy from one of those. I could have built an LED controller. I could have built a soil sensor, or a media player, or any of a dozen other things. I didn’t do anything at all.
But now that I’ve used the Aux-2 and dipped my toe into the ESPHome waters, maybe I will.

Fresh pouch milk sold under the Amul brand is set to become costlier across India from November 12, with the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF) increasing prices by approximately 4-5% across major variants. GCMMF, the apex dairy cooperative that markets milk and milk products under the Amul brand, said the revision affects some of its largest-selling fresh milk variants across operational markets. Under the revised pricing, Amul Taaza toned milk, which contains 3% milk fat, will cost ₹2 more per litre, marking a 3.3% increase. Amul Gold milk, containing 6% milk fat, will see a ₹4 per litre increase, or a 5.5% hike. Amul Gold will rise by ₹4 per litre, or 5.5%. GCMMF attributed the increase to higher milk production and processing costs, including the costs of fodder, cattle feed, packaging film and fuel. It also cited low and uneven rainfall. GCMMF said member unions increased the rates paid to farmers for milk by 4–5% over the past year. The consumer price revision is intended to help sustain those payments, with a major portion of the increase going to milk producers. The article specifies increases for Amul Taaza toned milk and Amul Gold. GCMMF said the revision affects some of its largest-selling fresh milk variants across its operational markets. The federation attributed the revision to rising input costs across dairy farming and commercial processing operations. "This price hike is being done due to the steep increase in input cost of milk production as well as processing," the dairy federation stated. GCMMF said the rising cost of agricultural inputs and commodities has increased expenditure on livestock management and daily operations. "There is a significant increase in cost of green and dry fodder, cattle feed ingredients like oil cake, maize and molasses, milk packaging film and fuel during the year," the statement added. The federation also cited challenging climatic conditions and uneven rainfall across agricultural regions as factors behind the decision. "In the current challenging environmental circumstances due to low and uneven rainfall in Gujarat as well as many parts of India, we are constrained to increase the consumer price of milk to pay better prices to our producers and support them in these difficult times," Amul said. The federation said its member unions have raised milk procurement rates paid to farmers by 4-5% over the past year. According to GCMMF, the latest consumer price revision is intended to help sustain these payments to milk producers. "It is important to note that 80% of the revenue collected from consumers through the Amul co-operative structure is returned to our 36 lakh milk producers," the company said. The cooperative added that a significant share of the increase in selling prices would be passed on to milk producers. "A major portion of the increase in the selling price of milk will go back to the milk producers and they will continue to be encouraged to increase milk production," the federation stated. Norwegian journalist Helle Lyng, who works for the Oslo-based daily newspaper Dagsavisen, has said that she has been stopped from coming to India despite having a valid visa.
“I got a visa to India and was supposed to leave this morning to attend the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad. I had been invited as a panellist and speaker on the future of media and press freedom. But «orders from above» in the Ministry of Home Affairs have cancelled my visa,” she said in a post on X, on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
“I was supposed to speak on media, press freedom and democracy and how they are intertwined,” she spoke in the video message where she puts the onus on India’s Home Minister Amit Shah to let her come as 48 hours are still there for her session.
She linked the refusal to let her into India to the freedom of press question she posed in Norway to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in May 2026.
Ms. Lyng has been listed as a speaker on Day 2 of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on November 14 in a session that will have Leonard Novy, director, Institute for Media and Communications, Sangeeta Baruah Pisharoty, president of the Press Club of India and Francesco Lapenta director of Institute of Future and Innovation Studies. The session will be moderated by Pawan Khera, MP and chairperson of INC Communications.
The Indian Embassy in Norway has not released any statement about the denial of permission. “The embassy in Norway is not at fault. They were truly nice and helpful during the process. It is the Ministry of Home Affairs that has ruined the trip by denying me entry even though I have gotten a visa and had political clearance for the conference,” she wrote in another social media past.

Randall England, an actor, model, writer and producer who appeared in TV shows including “General Hospital,” died Sept. 25 in Los Angeles, his family has announced. He was 75.
England began his career in 1978 with an uncredited role in the TV movie “Ruby and Oswalk” before landing an episode of the TV series “This Is the Life” in 1984. That same year, England was cast as “General Hospital” villain Jack Slater, and went on to appear on more than 30 episodes of the long-running soap opera. He appeared in two episodes of “Baywatch” in the late 1990s, and also voiced the character of Butler in the 2008 film “Beverly Hills Chihuahua.”
His last credit was for the 2018 film “Shiner,” and his producing work included the documentary The Needs of Kim Stanley. On stage, England appeared in productions of “All My Sons,” “The Glass Menagerie” and “The Three Sisters,” the latter of which he won a Drama League Award for best ensemble cast.
England was born on September 22, 1951, in Oklahoma City and graduated from the University of Oklahoma. He began modeling in the early 1970s and went on to work in New York, London, Zurich, Milan and Los Angeles. He studied acting with Kim Stanley and Stella Adler before building a career across television, film and theater.
He is survived by daughter Micaela Reed (Sam); grandchildren Katherine and Julian; mother Catherine Burgess; sister Linda Baker; and extended family.
While England’s family did not confirm his cause of death, they noted that memorial donations can be made to the Esophageal Cancer Action Network (ECAN).

Five arrested for allegedly desecrating Santal place of worship in Odisha's Keonjhar
The arrest came 12 days after the alleged incident was reported and almost three weeks after it occurred.
Odisha Police have arrested five persons for allegedly desecrating a sacred place of worship of the Santal community in Basantpur village of Keonjhar district,
The accused, identified as Chandan Sethy, Dibyajyoti Puhan, Akshay Kumar Sahoo, Suresh Mallick and Srichandan Puhan, were arrested by Ghasipura police on Tuesday.
The arrest came 12 days after the alleged incident was reported and almost three weeks after it occurred.
What allegedly happened
According to the FIR lodged by tribal villagers on October 29, the incident occurred on October 23 when members of the Santal community were worshipping at a sacred grove, locally known as Jaher Than. The complaint alleged that around 15 to 20 people, allegedly armed with knives, iron rods and sticks, barged into the place of worship and abused the worshippers.
When some women tried to resist the intruders, they were allegedly manhandled and subjected to inappropriate behaviour, the FIR stated. The attackers also allegedly dragged two youths along with their motorcycles for around 30 to 40 metres while leaving the spot, leaving them injured.
The complainants further alleged that the villagers were threatened with the discontinuation of their subsidised rice quota and government allowances if they reported the incident to the police.
Rabi Hembrum, one of the villagers, alleged that police had refused to register a separate FIR over the desecration of the Jaher Than and clubbed the matter with the case relating to the assault on villagers.
Anandpur sub-divisional police officer Kamal Lochan Panda said an investigation into the incident was underway.
Political turn
The incident triggered a political controversy, with a BJD delegation led by former minister and the party's Tribal Cell president Sudam Marndi alleging that people associated with the Bajrang Dal were behind the attack and demanding an independent investigation.
"When the chief minister himself belongs to the Santal community, the attack on tribals clearly demonstrates how unsafe the communities have become in the state," the BJD said in a statement.
No reaction from the Bajrang Dal or the ruling BJP is available so far.

Iran threatens to target US bases in Europe in chilling new threat
Iran has threatened to hit any European base which houses American aircrafts

An Iranian official has threatened strikes on US bases in Europe if Donald Trump launches new strikes against Iran.
Speaking to Al Mayadeen, a Beirut-based news channel with links to Hezbollah, Iranian Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said that any base which American aircrafts take off from are at risk of being attacked, according to Iran International.
“If the Americans make a mistake and attack us, we will not limit ourselves to nearby bases,” said Rezaei.
“We may even target some American military bases in European countries.”
This statement comes as President Donald Trump said future strikes on Iran are “unlikely”, but then added that the U.S. is "locked and loaded" if the situation does change, per the BBC.
Although Iranian officials have expressed doubt over the president’s statement, Trump may be serious about ending the war with Iran given the anti-war sentiment expressed by midterm election voters.
Many newly elected Democrats have said they will vote to end the war, and Vice President JD Vance told the press that he believes the war was the central cause of the Republicans’ seismic defeat in the midterms.
This warning over Iranian attacks on European military bases is coming from an official source. However, three men who are accused of being Iran-backed operatives are currently facing charges in the U.S. for attempting a terror attack on RAF Fairford, an airforce base in the U.K. which held American planes and hosted American service members.
The U.S. has now removed its bombers from the base. Iran has denied any involvement in the alleged plot.
The U.S. currently has 31 bases in Europe, and also shares 18 bases with European allies.
There were approximately 84,000 U.S. service members across the United States European Command (EUCOM) area of responsibility as of early 2025, according to data from the Center for European Policy Analysis.
The U.S. Air Force operates in the UK out of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall. However, the U.S. armed forces removed several aircraft from RAF Mildenhall on November 10th amid unspecified threats.
The threat to bomb military bases in Europe is not the only major threat made by Iran against the Trump administration in recent weeks.
U.S. Treasurer Scott Bessent had to move out of his D.C. home and on to a military base in early November due to threats from Iran, according to the New York Times.
Bessent has been leading financial pressure such as increased sanctions against the nation. It is unclear how severe the threats are at this time.

At St. Joseph’s Church in Kuriachira, Thrissur, Keralam, faith and fitness go hand in hand. An open gym on the church premises is drawing parishioners of all ages to stretch, sweat and stay fit. The unusual initiative is adding a healthy new dimension to church life.
Set up in a corner of the church campus, the facility has quickly become a meeting point for fitness enthusiasts. With no fixed timings, parishioners can drop in at their convenience, with many heading to the gym after attending Holy Mass. The altar boys, numbering around 60, are among its regular users. Parents also bring their young children, while senior citizens use the basic equipment to stay active.
Roots in fitness routine of vicar
The initiative has its roots in the personal fitness routine of the church’s vicar, Fr. Frederick Eluvathingal, 69. A footballer and basketball player during his student days, he has never allowed age or a demanding schedule to come in the way of exercise.
“I have been working out for the past 51 years, ever since my days at the Papal Seminary in Pune,” he says. His fitness routine continued during his higher studies in Rome and Jerusalem and his church assignments in Australia.
When he arrived at Kuriachira more than a year ago, he began looking for a suitable space to continue his regular exercises, including push-ups and pull-ups. Parallel bars were installed first, followed by a basketball hoop. The idea gradually grew into a community gym.
“I wanted to create a space where people could develop the habit of working out. We generally do not have a strong workout culture. If people can fit in some basic exercise when they come to church, they may gradually make fitness part of their lives,” he says.
The need is particularly pressing at a time when lifestyle diseases and obesity are on the rise. The initiative also seeks to draw more youngsters into church activities and channel their energy into constructive pursuits.
The parish welcomed the proposal, and a space around a well on the church premises was chosen for the facility. The limited space available in Kuriachira meant that the gym had to be modest, but the response has been encouraging.
“Within a week of starting the gym, quite a few people began coming here. If the demand grows, we will have to think about expanding the facility,” says P.R. Wilson, one of the church trustees.
For regular user John Vazhappilly, a real estate broker who lives nearby, the gym has come as a timely help. “I have been coming here every evening for the past week. After an accident and surgery, the muscles in my leg became weak. I want to strengthen them. This is a comfortable place to exercise, with fresh air and an open campus,” he says.
‘A form of spiritual service’
The church sees the initiative as more than a fitness facility. “We want to groom a healthy generation. Many people suffer from lifestyle diseases, while youngsters often turn to private fitness centres. We felt that providing basic facilities here would benefit the community. Spirituality is also about nurturing a healthy mind and body. We consider this a form of spiritual service,” says assistant vicar Fr. Jees Akkara.
For Fr. Eluvathingal, there is another purpose. “Youngsters rarely come to church or participate in its activities these days. This is also an opportunity to bring more of them into the church community,” he says.

Russell Brand, who was convicted of rape last week in London, posted on X Wednesday that his Instagram account has been removed by Meta.
Brand posted a screenshot reading, “We disabled your account. Our technology found your account, or your activity on it, doesn’t follow our rules.”
“We suspended your page. This is because Russell Brand goes against our community standards,” reads the screenshot from Brand’s now-removed Instagram profile page.
The British comedian was sentenced Monday to 10 years and six months in prison after being convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault.
Brand’s X page, with 10 million followers, is still active. “There never was a Russell Brand, according to @Meta. Thank God for @elonmusk. Stay tuned,” he wrote on X Wednesday.
Brand’s account was taken down because it “violates our policies,” a Meta spokesperson confirmed to TMZ.
After Brand’s comedy and movie appearances tapered off, he started a YouTube channel which during the COVID pandemic became increasingly right-wing and full of conspiracy theories.
He was accused of sexual misconduct multiple times before finally being charged in 2025. In 2023, YouTube suspended monetization of his account.
Judge Joel Bennathan began his sentencing remarks Monday by saying, “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. You were clever and, in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. You had also become a sexual predator.”
“No doubt your companions thought it was outrageous laddish behavior that only you could get away with: It was outrageous and possibly laddish, but also a criminal sexual offense, and as it turns out you haven’t got away with it,” the judge noted.
London’s Metropolitan Police said that Brand is being investigated on further allegations of rape from two other women.

Microsoft's Automatic Super Resolution is now officially out for the ROG Xbox Ally X
It’s the company’s response to NVIDIA’s DLSS and other similar upscaling tech.
Back in April, Microsoft revealed that it had started testing Automatic Super Resolution (Auto SR) on the ROG Xbox Ally X. Now, the upscaling technology designed to compete with similar video game tools like NVIDIA's DLSS, is officially rolling out to the Ally X, ROG Xbox Ally X20 and select Windows Copilot+ PCs powered by AMD Ryzen. The official version of Auto SR works even when the console is undocked, unlike the preview version that doesn't support handheld play.
Auto SR allows the docked handheld to offer "1440p-like detail alongside smooth framerates on larger screens." It means it can upscale your game up to 1440p in resolution to make it look sharper if you're playing on the TV. While that was its original purpose, Microsoft said it made the upscaling tech available even in handheld mode due to popular demand. Auto SR can "smooth things out" if a demanding game "feels a little choppy on the go," the company wrote in its announcement.
The new version of Auto SR works with games running at 1080p on default, which would be most games played on the ASUS consoles. During its preview, you'd had to lower the game's resolution before the tech could kick in. Now that's no longer necessary. Microsoft warned, however, that when using 1080p on handheld, "performance may not be as optimal as other configurations." You're bound to still see visual quality improvements, though, especially for older games.
In addition, the new Auto SR can reach framerates up to 120 fps, wheres the preview version could only hit between 60 to 75 fps. Microsoft explained that it would make fast-past and competitive games like shooters feel and look smoother on screen. Finally, Auto SDR now supports HDR visuals. Both the higher framerate capability, which Microsoft calls "Performance Mode," and HDR support will be rolling out with future Windows updates.

Democrats face backlash after missing Hegseth impeachment vote
Republicans in the US House of Representatives blocked an attempt to impeach Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, sparking a flurry of criticism online, as 11 Democrats failed to attend the vote.
The chamber voted 211 to 204 to refer the charges to the House Judiciary Committee, where they could remain indefinitely for the duration of this Congress’s term, essentially killing the resolution for now.
The articles were spearheaded by Republican Thomas Massie and backed heavily by Democrats, accusing Hegseth of carrying out unlawful orders and waging unconstitutional wars in Iran and Venezuela.
Notably, there were 18 representatives missing during the votes - seven Republicans and 11 Democrats. The Democrats missing included California's Nancy Pelosi; Michigan’s Haley Stevens; New York’s Laura Gillen; California’s Lou Correa; New Mexico’s Melanie Stansbury; and several others.
Several party members and others heavily criticised the absentee Democrats online, who in response blamed traffic, Representative Mike Johnson closing the vote early, and having conflicting events.

When HIV was first discovered in the early 1980s, it was virtually a death sentence. Now, we have treatments that can keep it at bay and prevent it from progressing to AIDS — but for some people, the disease never progresses, even without treatment. These so-called elite controllers make up perhaps less than 0.5 percent of all HIV patients, and their survival could hold the secret to a lasting “functional” cure to the disease. In this month’s Highlight cover story, Diana Kwon investigates what makes “elite controllers” different, how their HIV resistance functions, and whether it’s replicable for others. Researchers at Google DeepMind have unveiled a new AI model designed to unravel how changes in our DNA affect different cells, giving scientists a more detailed view of a notoriously difficult problem that could hold important clues to the causes of disease — and point the way to new treatments.
Google’s AlphaGenome 2 zooms in on the cellular roots of disease
DeepMind’s new DNA model better predicts how mutations affect different cells, potentially opening paths to treatment.
AlphaGenome 2 is the successor to DeepMind’s genome-predicting AI model AlphaGenome, which was released last year. While nearly every cell in the human body carries the same DNA, different types of cells — from heart muscle cells and skin cells to immune cells fighting an infection — switch different genes on and off, and those patterns can change depending on what a cell is doing. As a result, the same genetic variant can have very different effects depending on the type and state of the cell.
The new model is designed to capture those differences, predicting the effects of genetic variants on individual cell types and states. Google said in a blog post published Wednesday that it offers a much finer-grained view than broader models like AlphaGenome, potentially revealing disease-relevant effects in specific cells that might otherwise go unnoticed.
AlphaGenome 2 was trained on more than 100 million individual cell profiles across 68 tissues to give it that more detailed view. DeepMind says the model effectively turns static cell atlases — huge data repositories that map and catalog individual cells in detail — “into a predictive engine for human genetics.” According to the company, AlphaGenome 2 identifies nearly twice as many variants that can change gene expression in cells than its previous state-of-the-art model.
Notably, the researchers found that AlphaGenome 2 could also make predictions about new types of cells and biological states without needing to be retrained. It could also identify gaps in experimental data, potentially helping scientists decide what to investigate next in the lab.
For Adam Gayoso, a research scientist at Google DeepMind involved in the project, the big breakthrough is “tying human genetics to cell biology.” AlphaGenome 2 gives researchers a way to drill down on genetic variants identified in large populations, to see what effects they may be having on a cellular level, and potentially connect those effects to disease, he told The Verge.
Google DeepMind’s genomics lead Žiga Avsec told The Verge that this specificity is important if you have a goal like figuring out how to treat a particular disease. “When you develop drugs, you’re targeting specific proteins and specific cell types,” he explained, which makes having this kind of granularity vital.
Building a model like AlphaGenome 2 has only recently become possible thanks to new technologies that can capture individual cells and their states at high resolution and create the vast datasets needed to train it, Avsec said. DeepMind is now working to improve its genetics models by generating more data, including for cell states that aren’t represented well today. Avsec said future versions could also potentially be trained on data “across multiple species,” giving the models a broader view of biology. Longer term, he said models like AlphaGenome 2 could feed into efforts to create “virtual cells,” digital simulations designed to mimic biological systems.
Although Avsec said he views AlphaGenome 2 as a successor to AlphaGenome, it isn’t replacing it any time soon. He said its more detailed predictions come at a computational cost and are “more expensive” to produce than those of its predecessor, he said. Those demands would have made it impractical to use AlphaGenome 2 to produce the genome-wide Atlas covering “every possible DNA letter change in the human genome” that DeepMind released in September.
Google says it is making AlphaGenome 2 available for non-commercial research via the AlphaGenome API from today, with a limited “private preview” for commercial research.
The model is the latest in a growing array of efforts by Google and rival AI labs to use the technology to tackle major problems in science and medicine. Pushmeet Kohli, who heads DeepMind’s AI for science research, has hinted that more impressive scientific results are on the way, and the organization is expected to open an automated materials science lab in the UK soon. Anthropic, meanwhile, has been experimenting with drug design and given Claude a wet lab, while OpenAI has been mowing down an impressive amount of longstanding problems in mathematics and related fields.

Amid rising concerns over the spread of Ebola to neighbouring countries, the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, A.P., has stepped up surveillance at three airports — Bhogapuram (Visakhapatnam), Vijayawada, and Tirupati — as a precautionary measure.
According to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, an official U.S. government website, the outbreak is spreading “substantially faster” than previous Ebola outbreaks and is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.
In this connection, the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare held a video conference on November 5, Thursday, with State governments regarding the precautionary measures to be taken. The Union government officials also reviewed the implementation of the Ebola guidelines.
A.P. Health Secretary G. Veerapandian, who took part in the conference, explained the arrangements being made in the State as part of the preparedness.
Arrangements at 5 govt. hospitals
According to a release from the department on Thursday, isolation beds at five government hospitals, medical personnel, emergency equipment have been readied. Mr. Veerapandian informed the Union government that medical teams had been deputed at three airports to screen passengers arriving from Ebola-affected countries for any symptoms. Similar arrangements are also in place at Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Nellore ports.
A total of 46 beds, 3,288 personal protective equipment (PPE) kits, 104 sample collection kits and five ambulances had been kept ready to deal with any eventuality, he said.
Mock drill
A mock drill will be conducted on November 12 to assess preparedness at the State and district levels, he said, adding that the departments concerned would be alerted to ensure that the guidelines are followed.
The Central officials have advised that passengers arriving from Ebola-affected countries be screened for symptoms, and those who had direct contact with infected persons be placed under observation. The medical teams should verify travel history of even those who do not exhibit any symptoms, the officials said.
If any person exhibits any symptoms, they should be taken to the hospital where isolation beds have been set up, the officials told the States.
As of October 31, Democratic Republic of the Congo reported 10,467 cases and 5,103 deaths, Kenya nine cases and two deaths, Uganda 20 cases and two deaths, Nigeria one case and France one case. Overall, 10,498 confirmed cases and 5,107 deaths were reported across five countries.
